64414.e: Ganesha is seen as the god of wisdom and cleverness. That is why schoolchildren and learners like him too.
64414.m: Ganesha is the god of cleverness.

64415.q: What colour is Krishna's skin often in pictures?
64415.e: Krishna is often painted with blue or dark skin. The colour is a reminder of the sky and the sea.
64415.m: In pictures Krishna often has blue skin.

64416.e: In many pictures Krishna plays a flute. With his music he is said to have enchanted everyone.

64417.q: Which feather does Krishna often wear in his hair?
64417.e: Krishna often wears a colourful peacock feather in his hair. This makes him easy to recognise.
64417.m: Krishna wears a peacock feather in his hair.

64418.q: Which animals did Krishna look after as a boy?
64418.e: According to the stories, Krishna grew up with cowherds. He looked after the cows and played his flute.
64418.m: As a boy Krishna looked after cows.

64419.q: What did little Krishna love to pinch?
64419.e: Little Krishna secretly snacked on butter from the pots. That is why he is also called the butter thief.
64419.m: Little Krishna loved to pinch butter.

64420.q: What is Krishna's best friend called in many stories?
64420.e: In many songs and stories Radha is Krishna's dearest friend. The two are often shown together.

64421.q: Krishna is a form of which god?
64421.e: Hindus believe that the god Vishnu came to earth in different forms. Krishna is one of these forms.
64421.m: Krishna is a form of Vishnu.

64422.q: What do Hindus celebrate at the festival of Janmashtami?
64422.e: At Janmashtami Hindus celebrate the birth of Krishna. Many stay awake until midnight.
64422.m: At Janmashtami Hindus celebrate Krishna's birthday.

64423.q: With what skin colour is Krishna often shown in pictures?
64423.e: Krishna is usually painted with blue or dark skin. According to the story he was born in Mathura in northern India.
64423.m: Krishna is often shown with blue skin.

64424.q: Which country does the Ganges mainly flow through?
64424.e: The Ganges is a big river in India. At the end it flows through Bangladesh into the sea.
64424.m: The Ganges flows mainly through India.

64425.q: Why do many Hindus bathe in the Ganges?
64425.e: For Hindus the Ganges is a holy river. Bathing in it is believed to cleanse the soul.
64425.m: The Ganges is holy for Hindus.

64426.q: In which mountain range does the Ganges rise?
64426.e: The Ganges rises from a glacier high in the Himalayas. From there it flows down to the plains.
64426.m: The Ganges comes from the Himalayas.

64427.q: Where does the Ganges flow in the end?
64427.e: The Ganges flows into the Bay of Bengal. That is part of the Indian Ocean.
64427.m: The Ganges flows into the sea.

64428.q: Which holy city lies on the Ganges?
64428.e: Varanasi is one of the holiest cities for Hindus. Lots of steps lead down to the Ganges there.

64429.q: What is the Ganges for many Hindus?
64429.e: Hindus worship the river as the goddess Ganga. People bring her flowers and lights.
64429.m: For Hindus the Ganges is a goddess.

64430.q: What do people put on the Ganges in the evening?
64430.e: In the evening people put little lights and flowers on the water. They then float away down the river.
64430.m: In the evening little lights float on the Ganges.

64431.q: Where does the lotus flower grow?
64431.e: The lotus flower grows in ponds and lakes. Its roots are in the mud at the bottom.
64431.m: The lotus flower grows in water.

64432.q: What is the lotus flower a symbol of?
64432.e: The lotus grows out of mud and still blooms perfectly clean. That is why it stands for purity.
64432.m: The lotus flower stands for purity.

64433.q: What happens to water on a lotus leaf?
64433.e: On a lotus leaf, drops of water simply roll off. They take the dirt with them.
64433.m: Water rolls off a lotus leaf.

64434.q: The lotus flower is the national flower of which country?
64434.e: The lotus flower is regarded as India's national flower. You can see it in pictures everywhere there.
64434.m: The lotus flower is the national flower of India.

64435.q: What does the god Vishnu often hold in one hand in pictures?
64435.e: In pictures Vishnu has four arms. In one hand he almost always holds a lotus flower.
64435.m: In pictures Vishnu often holds a lotus flower.

64436.q: Where are the round leaves of the lotus flower?
64436.e: The big round leaves float on the water or rise above it. The flower stands high above the water.
64436.m: Lotus leaves lie on the water.

64437.q: Which part of the lotus plant is often eaten in Asia?
64437.e: In Asia the thick root of the lotus plant is boiled or fried. The seeds can be eaten too.
64437.m: The root of the lotus plant can be eaten.

64438.q: What colour are lotus flowers often?
64438.e: Lotus flowers are often pink or white. Some are white with pink tips.
64438.m: Lotus flowers are often pink or white.

64439.q: What do you do with your hands for namaste?
64439.e: For namaste you press both palms flat together. You need both hands for it.
64439.m: For namaste you put your hands together.

64440.e: Namaste is a greeting in India and Nepal. You say it kindly to other people.
64440.m: Namaste is a greeting from India.

64441.e: You can say namaste to greet someone and to say goodbye. So it works like “hello” and “goodbye”.
64441.m: Namaste is said when coming and going.

64442.e: The word comes from an old language of India. It means roughly “I bow to you”.
64442.m: Namaste means roughly “I bow to you”.

64443.q: Where do you hold your hands for namaste?
64443.e: The hands are pressed flat together in front of the chest. The fingers point upwards.
64443.m: For namaste your hands are in front of your chest.

64444.q: What do you do with your head for namaste?
64444.e: For the namaste greeting you bow your head a little. This shows respect.
64444.m: For namaste you bow your head slightly.

64445.q: Do you touch the other person when you say namaste?
64445.e: With namaste you do not touch the other person. You greet them only with your own hands.
64445.m: Namaste is a greeting without touching.

64446.q: Which old language does the word namaste come from?
64446.e: Sanskrit is a very old language of India. Many holy Hindu texts are written in it.

64447.e: A rangoli is a colourful pattern on the floor. It is laid out or sprinkled by hand.
64447.m: A rangoli is a colourful pattern on the floor.

64448.q: Where is a rangoli often made?
a: In front of the front door
64448.e: Rangolis often decorate the ground in front of the entrance. They are usually made early in the morning.
64448.m: A rangoli is often in front of the front door.

64449.q: What is a rangoli often made from?
64449.e: Coloured powder or coloured sand is sprinkled into a pattern. Petals are used too.
64449.m: Rangolis are often made from coloured powder.

64450.q: At which festival are especially many rangolis made?
64450.e: For Diwali many families decorate their entrance with a rangoli. It is meant to bring luck into the house.
64450.m: At Diwali there are especially many rangolis.

64451.q: Which parts of flowers are also used for a rangoli?
64451.e: Some rangolis are laid out with colourful petals. Then they smell lovely too.
64451.m: You can make a rangoli from petals.

64452.q: What do many rangoli patterns look like?
64452.e: Many rangolis are symmetrical, which means the same on all sides. Often you can see flowers, circles or stars.
64452.m: Many rangolis are the same on all sides.

64453.q: What is a rangoli usually sprinkled with?
64453.e: The powder is usually sprinkled onto the ground between the fingers. This makes fine lines.
64453.m: A rangoli is sprinkled with the fingers.

64454.q: Which powder from the kitchen is often used for a rangoli?
64454.e: Many rangolis are sprinkled with white rice flour. Small creatures such as ants may eat it.
64454.m: Rice flour is often used for rangolis.

64455.e: Puja is the Hindu word for worshipping the gods. People pray and bring offerings.
64455.m: Puja means worship of the gods.

64456.q: Where can a puja take place?
a: At home or in the temple
64456.e: Many Hindus have a small altar at home. They celebrate puja there and in the temple.
64456.m: A puja is held at home or in the temple.

64457.q: What is often brought as an offering at a puja?
64457.e: At a puja people give the gods flowers, fruit or sweets. This is a sign of thanks.
64457.m: At a puja people often give flowers.

64458.q: What is often lit at a puja?
64458.e: Incense sticks often burn at a puja. They smell nice and the smoke rises upwards.
64458.m: At a puja incense sticks are lit.

64459.q: What is waved in front of the image of the god at a puja?
64459.e: During aarti a small lamp is waved in a circle in front of the image of the god. People sing at the same time.
64459.m: At a puja a lamp is waved.

64460.q: What is often rung at a puja?
64460.e: At the start of a puja a small bell is often rung. It is meant to get the gods' attention.
64460.m: At a puja a small bell rings.

64461.q: What do you take off in front of the temple?
64461.e: In front of a Hindu temple you take off your shoes. This keeps the holy place clean.
64461.m: You take off your shoes in front of the temple.

64462.q: What happens to the food after the puja?
64462.e: The blessed food after the puja is called prasad. It is handed out to everyone and eaten.
64462.m: After the puja the food is shared.

64463.e: Om is a holy word and a holy sound. Hindus say or chant it when they pray.

64464.q: When do many Hindus say Om?
a: At the start of a prayer
64464.e: Many prayers begin with the sound Om. It is often said at the end too.

64465.q: What does Om sound like when it is chanted?
64465.e: Om is usually chanted long and calmly. The sound hums through the whole body.
64465.m: Om is chanted long and calmly.

64466.q: During which activity is Om often chanted?
64466.e: Many yoga classes begin or end with everyone chanting Om together. This is meant to be calming.
64466.m: Om is often chanted in yoga.

64467.q: According to old teaching, how many sounds make up Om?
64467.e: According to old teaching, Om is made up of the three sounds A, U and M.
64467.m: Om is made up of the sounds A, U and M.

64468.q: What do you call a holy word that is often repeated, like Om?
64468.e: A mantra is a holy word or a short saying. You say or chant it again and again.
64468.m: A holy word that is repeated is called a mantra.

64469.q: Where do you often see the Om symbol?
64469.e: The Om symbol can be seen in temples, on altars and in pictures. It is an important Hindu symbol.
64469.m: You often see the Om symbol in temples.

64470.q: In which other religion is Om also holy?
64470.e: Om is not only important for Hindus. It is also seen as holy in Buddhism, in Jainism and by Sikhs.
64470.m: Om is also holy in Buddhism.

64471.e: The bindi is a dot placed on the forehead. You can see it well from the front.
64471.m: The bindi is worn on the forehead.

64472.q: What colour is a bindi traditionally?
64472.e: Traditionally the bindi is a red dot. Today there are bindis in many colours.

64473.q: What does the word bindi mean?
64473.e: The word comes from an old language of India. It means dot or drop.

64474.q: Traditionally, what does a red bindi show for many women?
64474.e: A bride is given a red bindi at her wedding. After that, many married women go on wearing it.
64474.m: Traditionally a red bindi shows that a woman is married.

64475.e: It is mainly women and girls who wear a bindi. Today it is often worn as jewellery too.
64475.m: Mainly women and girls wear a bindi.

64476.q: What is an easy way to wear a bindi today?
64476.e: In the past the bindi was painted on with powder. Today there are also small stick-on dots, often with glitter.
64476.m: Today you can stick a bindi on.

64478.q: What else can a bindi stand for today?
64478.e: Today many people simply wear a bindi as pretty jewellery. It often matches the colour of their clothes.
64478.m: Today a bindi is often jewellery too.

64479.q: Which country does yoga come from?
64479.e: Yoga began in India. It is very old.

64480.e: Yoga has been practised in India for well over 2000 years. Old texts describe it.

64481.q: On which day is International Yoga Day?
64481.e: The United Nations declared 21 June Yoga Day. It has been celebrated since 2015.

64482.q: What are the body positions in yoga called?
64482.e: The yoga positions are called asanas. You hold them still for a while.

64483.q: What do you pay special attention to in yoga?
64483.e: In yoga you breathe calmly and carefully. Breathing and movement go together.
64483.m: In yoga you pay attention to your breathing.

64484.q: What is the yoga exercise that many people do in the morning called?
64484.e: The sun salutation is a series of positions one after the other. Many people do it in the morning.
64484.m: The sun salutation greets the sun.

64485.q: In which yoga position do you stand on one leg?
64485.e: In the tree you stand on one leg. The other foot rests against your leg and your arms go up.
64485.m: In the tree you stand on one leg.

64486.q: Which animal is a yoga position lying on your tummy named after?
64486.e: In the cobra you lie on your tummy and lift your upper body. It looks like a snake with its head raised.
64486.m: The cobra is a yoga position on your tummy.

64487.q: What do people usually do yoga on?
64487.e: Yoga is usually done on a thin mat. That way you do not slip.
64487.m: Yoga is usually done on a mat.

64488.q: What was Buddha called before he became Buddha?
64488.e: At birth Buddha was given the name Siddhartha Gautama. Only later was he called Buddha.

64489.q: What was Siddhartha as a child?
64489.e: Siddhartha was the son of a king. He grew up as a prince in a beautiful palace.

64490.q: In which present-day country was Siddhartha born?
64490.e: Siddhartha was born in Lumbini. Today this place is in Nepal, near the border with India.
64490.m: Buddha's birthplace, Lumbini, is in Nepal.

64491.e: Buddha lived in India about 2500 years ago. The exact year is not known for certain.

64492.q: What was the name of Siddhartha's mother?
64492.e: His mother was Queen Maya. According to tradition she died shortly after his birth, so her sister brought him up.

64493.e: His father was King Suddhodana. He ruled over a small kingdom.

64494.q: What did Siddhartha's father want his son to become?
64494.e: His father wanted Siddhartha to become king one day. That is why he was meant to see nothing sad and stay in the palace.
64494.m: His father wanted Siddhartha to become king.

64495.q: Roughly how old did Buddha live to be?
64495.e: According to tradition, Buddha lived to be about 80. Until his death he travelled around teaching people.

64496.q: What did Siddhartha see on his third trip out of the palace?
64496.e: On his third trip Siddhartha saw a dead person. In this way he realised that every life comes to an end.
64496.m: On the third trip Siddhartha realised that every life ends.

64497.q: Who did Siddhartha see on his first trip out of the palace?
64497.e: First he saw a very old man. In this way he learned that all people grow old.
64497.m: On the first trip Siddhartha saw an old man.

64498.q: What did Siddhartha learn when he saw a sick person?
64498.e: In the palace he had never seen sick people. Now he understood that anyone can get ill.
64498.m: Siddhartha realised that anyone can get ill.

64499.q: Which person did Siddhartha see on his fourth trip out of the palace?
64499.e: Last of all he saw a calm monk. This monk showed him a way to deal with suffering.
64499.m: A peaceful monk showed Siddhartha a new way.

64500.q: Roughly how old was Siddhartha when he left the palace?
64500.e: According to tradition, Siddhartha left the palace at about 29. He wanted to find out how suffering can be overcome.
64500.m: Siddhartha left the palace at about 29.

64501.q: At what time of day did Siddhartha secretly leave the palace?
64501.e: Siddhartha rode away secretly at night. Nobody was to stop him.
64501.m: Siddhartha secretly left the palace at night.

64502.q: Which animal did Siddhartha ride away from the palace on?
64502.e: He rode away on his white horse Kanthaka. His servant Channa went with him.
64502.m: Siddhartha rode away on his horse Kanthaka.

64503.q: What did Siddhartha cut off after leaving?
64503.e: Siddhartha cut off his long hair. This showed that he no longer wanted to be a prince.
64503.m: Siddhartha cut off his hair when he became a wanderer.

64504.q: Under which tree did Buddha find enlightenment?
64504.e: Siddhartha sat down under a big tree and stayed sitting there for a long time. Since then this tree has been called the Bodhi tree.
64504.m: Buddha became enlightened under the Bodhi tree.

64505.e: “Bodhi” means awakening or enlightenment. That is why the tree is called the Bodhi tree.

64506.q: What shape are the leaves of the Bodhi tree?
64506.e: The leaves are heart-shaped with a long tip. You often see them as a symbol in Buddhist pictures.
64506.m: The leaf of the Bodhi tree is heart-shaped.

64507.q: What kind of tree is the Bodhi tree?
64507.e: The Bodhi tree is a sacred fig. It belongs to the fig trees.
64507.m: The Bodhi tree is a fig tree.

64508.q: What is the place in India where the Bodhi tree stands called?
64508.e: The place is called Bodh Gaya and lies in the state of Bihar in eastern India. Many pilgrims visit it every year.
64508.m: The Bodhi tree stands in Bodh Gaya in India.

64509.q: What did Siddhartha do under the Bodhi tree?
64509.e: Siddhartha sat quietly under the tree and meditated. In doing so he saw the truth and became the Buddha.
64509.m: Siddhartha meditated under the Bodhi tree.

64510.q: Roughly how old was Siddhartha when he became enlightened?
64510.e: According to tradition, Siddhartha became enlightened at about 35. After that he taught for many more years.

64511.q: What is the name of the demon who disturbed Buddha under the tree?
64511.e: The demon Mara tried to distract Siddhartha with fear and temptations. But Siddhartha stayed calmly sitting.
64511.m: The demon Mara could not distract Buddha.

64512.q: In which country is there an ancient tree that grew from a cutting of the Bodhi tree?
64512.e: In Anuradhapura in Sri Lanka there is a tree that grew from a cutting of the Bodhi tree. It was planted over 2200 years ago.
64512.m: An ancient cutting of the Bodhi tree grows in Sri Lanka.

64513.q: What does Buddha have on his head on many statues?
64513.e: Many statues show a bump on the head that looks like a topknot of hair. It is a sign of his wisdom.
64513.m: The bump on the head of a Buddha statue stands for wisdom.

64514.q: Why does Buddha often have long earlobes on statues?
a: He wore heavy jewellery as a prince
64514.e: As a prince Siddhartha wore heavy gold earrings. These made his earlobes long.
64514.m: The long earlobes are a reminder of Buddha's life as a prince.

64515.q: How do the eyes of many Buddha statues look?
64515.e: The eyes are often half closed. This shows that Buddha is calmly looking inwards and meditating.
64515.m: Half-closed eyes show calm and meditation.

64516.q: In which position does a statue show Buddha shortly before his death?
64516.e: The reclining Buddha shows him at the end of his life. He lies calmly on his right side.
64516.m: The reclining Buddha shows Buddha at the end of his life.

64517.q: In which city is the famous reclining Buddha in the Wat Pho temple?
64517.e: In the Wat Pho temple in Bangkok, Thailand, there is a gilded reclining Buddha. It is about 46 metres long.
64517.m: The reclining Buddha of Wat Pho is in Bangkok.

64518.q: What colour are many Buddha statues in Thailand?
64518.e: Many statues in Thailand are gilded or gold-coloured. Gold shows how precious the teaching is.
64518.m: In Thailand many Buddha statues shine gold.

64519.q: In which country is the giant Leshan Buddha, carved into a cliff?
64519.e: The Leshan Giant Buddha in China is about 71 metres high. It was carved out of a cliff over 1200 years ago.
64519.m: The giant cliff Buddha of Leshan is in China.

64520.q: Who does the figure of the fat, laughing Buddha show?
64520.e: The laughing Buddha is called Budai and was a cheerful monk from China. He is not the Buddha Siddhartha.
64520.m: The laughing Buddha is a cheerful monk from China.

64521.q: What is Buddha showing when a statue shows him touching the earth with one hand?
a: He calls the earth as his witness
64521.e: When a demon disturbed him, Buddha touched the earth with his hand. He called on it as a witness to his enlightenment.
64521.m: With his hand on the ground, Buddha calls the earth as his witness.

64522.q: How does Buddha sit on many statues?
64522.e: Buddha usually sits on the ground with his legs crossed. This position is called the lotus position.
64522.m: In the lotus position you sit with crossed legs.

64523.q: What do the legs in the lotus position remind people of?
64523.e: The lotus position is named after the lotus flower. The legs and feet look like the petals of an open flower.
64523.m: The lotus position is named after the lotus flower.

64524.q: Where are the feet in the full lotus position?
64524.e: In the full lotus position each foot rests on the opposite thigh. The soles of the feet point upwards.
64524.m: In the full lotus position the feet rest on the thighs.

64525.q: What is the lotus position often used for?
64525.e: In the lotus position you sit calmly and upright. This makes it good for meditating.
64525.m: The lotus position is used for meditating.

64526.q: Why is the lotus flower a beautiful symbol in Buddhism?
a: It blooms pure out of the mud
64526.e: The lotus flower grows in muddy water, but its flower stays clean. In the same way a person can become good and pure.
64526.m: The lotus flower blooms clean out of the mud.

64527.q: Where are the hands often placed when meditating in the lotus position?
64527.e: The hands often rest calmly in the lap, one hand in the other. The thumbs touch lightly.
64527.m: When meditating, the hands often rest in the lap.

64528.q: How should your back be in the lotus position?
64528.e: When meditating you sit with a straight back. This helps you breathe calmly and well.
64528.m: In the lotus position you keep your back straight.

64529.q: What does Buddha sit on in many pictures?
64529.e: In many pictures Buddha sits on a big lotus flower. It serves as his throne.
64529.m: In many pictures Buddha sits on a lotus flower.

64531.q: What colour are the robes of Tibetan monks usually?
64531.e: Tibetan monks usually wear dark red robes. They often wear yellow cloth with them.
64531.m: Tibetan monks usually wear dark red robes.

64532.q: What colour do Zen monks in Japan often wear?
64532.e: Zen monks in Japan often wear black robes. So the colour is not the same everywhere.
64532.m: Zen monks in Japan often wear black robes.

64533.q: What do Buddhist monks do with their hair?
64533.e: Monks shave their heads. This shows that appearance is not important to them.

64534.q: What do monks in Thailand collect in their bowls in the morning?
64534.e: In the morning monks walk through the streets with a bowl. People give them food.
64534.m: In the morning monks collect food in a bowl.

64535.q: How many pieces does a monk's robe in Thailand usually have?
64535.e: A monk in Thailand usually has three cloths: an under-robe, an upper robe and a cloak. They are wrapped around the body.
64535.m: A monk's robe is usually made of three cloths.

64536.q: What were monks' robes sewn from in the past?
64536.e: In the past monks sewed their robes from old scraps of cloth. They were meant to live simply and own nothing expensive.
64536.m: In the past monks' robes were sewn from scraps of cloth.

64537.q: What do you call a young monk who is still learning?
64537.e: A young monk who is still learning is called a novice. In Thailand many boys become novices for a while.
64537.m: A young monk who is learning is called a novice.

64538.q: In which region do you see especially many prayer flags?
64538.e: Prayer flags come from Tibet and often flutter in the Himalayas. You see them on passes, bridges and mountains.
64538.m: Prayer flags often flutter in the Himalayas.

64539.q: How many colours do Tibetan prayer flags have?
64539.e: Tibetan prayer flags have five colours: blue, white, red, green and yellow. They always hang in this order.
64539.m: Tibetan prayer flags have five colours.

64540.q: According to the belief, what carries the good wishes of the prayer flags onwards?
64540.e: Prayers and wishes are written on the flags. The wind is meant to carry them all over the world.
64540.m: The wind carries the wishes of the prayer flags into the world.

64541.q: What does the blue prayer flag stand for?
64541.e: Each colour stands for something in nature. Blue stands for the sky.
64541.m: The blue prayer flag stands for the sky.

64542.q: What does the red prayer flag stand for?
64542.e: The red flag stands for fire. Green stands for water and yellow for earth.
64542.m: The red prayer flag stands for fire.

64543.q: Which animal is printed in the middle of many prayer flags?
64543.e: Many flags have a horse printed on them, the wind horse. It is meant to bring luck and good wishes.
64543.m: Many prayer flags show a wind horse.

64544.q: What do people do with prayer flags when they fade?
64544.e: The flags stay up until wind and weather bleach them. Then new flags are hung up beside them.
64544.m: Prayer flags may fade in the wind.

64545.q: Where can you sometimes see prayer flags in Switzerland too?
64545.e: Many mountaineers bring prayer flags back from the Himalayas. That is why they sometimes flutter at mountain huts in the Alps too.
64545.m: Prayer flags sometimes hang in the Swiss Alps too.

64546.q: What do you do with a prayer wheel?
64546.e: A prayer wheel is a cylinder that can be turned. You turn it while thinking of good wishes.

64547.q: In which direction do you turn a prayer wheel?
64547.e: Prayer wheels are turned clockwise. This way the prayer is read in the right order.

64548.q: What is hidden inside a prayer wheel?
64548.e: Inside the prayer wheel there is a roll of paper with a prayer written on it many times. Each turn counts like a spoken prayer.
64548.m: Inside the prayer wheel there is paper with prayers.

64549.q: Which region do prayer wheels mainly come from?
64549.e: Prayer wheels are especially important in Tibetan Buddhism. You see them in Tibet, Nepal and Bhutan.
64549.m: Prayer wheels belong mainly to Tibet.

64550.q: Which prayer is often written on a Tibetan prayer wheel?
64550.e: The best-known prayer is “Om mani padme hum”. It wishes compassion for all beings.
64550.m: Prayer wheels often have “Om mani padme hum” on them.

64551.q: What turns some big prayer wheels in the mountains without people?
64551.e: Some prayer wheels stand over a stream. The flowing water turns them without stopping.
64551.m: Some prayer wheels are turned by water.

64552.q: Where are there often long rows of prayer wheels?
64552.e: At many temples there are whole rows of prayer wheels along the wall. People walk past and turn each one.
64552.m: Along temple walls there are often many prayer wheels in a row.

64553.q: How do you hold a small prayer wheel?
64553.e: There are small prayer wheels with a handle. You hold them in one hand and let them spin.
64553.m: You hold a small prayer wheel in your hand.

64554.q: What shape does a stupa usually have?
64554.e: A stupa is a building with a round dome. It often has a spire on top.
64554.m: A stupa is usually shaped like a dome.

64555.q: What is often kept in a stupa?
64555.e: Many stupas contain relics, that is, remains of Buddha or holy people. That is why stupas are holy places.
64555.m: Relics are often kept in stupas.

64556.q: How do believers walk around a stupa?
64556.e: Believers walk round the stupa clockwise. In this way they always have it on their right-hand side.
64556.m: You walk round a stupa clockwise.

64557.q: What is painted on the Boudhanath stupa in Nepal?
64557.e: Large eyes are painted on the tower of the Boudhanath stupa. They look in all four directions.
64557.m: The Boudhanath stupa has painted eyes.

64558.q: In which city is the Boudhanath stupa?
64558.e: The Boudhanath stupa is in Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal. It is one of the biggest stupas in the world.
64558.m: The Boudhanath stupa is in Kathmandu.

64559.q: In which country is the Borobudur temple with its many stupas?
64559.e: Borobudur on the island of Java in Indonesia is the biggest Buddhist temple in the world. Many small stupas stand on it.
64559.m: Borobudur with its many stupas is in Indonesia.

64560.q: What is the building in East Asia that developed from the stupa called?
64560.e: In China and Japan the stupa became a tall tower with many roofs. It is called a pagoda.
64560.m: The pagoda developed from the stupa.

64561.q: What colour is the famous Shwedagon Pagoda in Myanmar?
64561.e: The Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon is covered in gold. It shines far out over the city.
64561.m: The Shwedagon Pagoda in Myanmar shines gold.

64562.q: In which country are the ancient stupas of Sanchi?
64562.e: The stupas of Sanchi in India are among the oldest Buddhist buildings. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
64562.m: The ancient stupas of Sanchi are in India.

64563.q: What do Buddhists celebrate at the festival of Vesak?
64563.e: At Vesak Buddhists remember Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death. All three events are celebrated on one day.
64563.m: At Vesak people celebrate Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death.

64564.q: In which month is Vesak often held?
64564.e: Vesak is in the lunar month of Vesakha, which usually falls in May. That is why the date is different every year.

64565.q: At which phase of the moon is Vesak celebrated?
64565.e: Vesak is celebrated on the day of the full moon. Many Buddhist festivals follow the moon.
64565.m: Vesak is celebrated at full moon.

64566.q: What do people in Sri Lanka hang up at Vesak?
64566.e: In Sri Lanka people decorate the streets with lots of colourful lanterns. At night everything shines brightly.
64566.m: At Vesak many lanterns shine in Sri Lanka.

64567.q: What is poured over a small Buddha figure on Buddha's birthday?
64567.e: Water is poured over a small figure of the baby Buddha. This is a reminder of his birth.
64567.m: On Buddha's birthday water is poured over a small Buddha figure.

64568.q: Which organisation declared Vesak an international day in 1999?
64568.e: The United Nations (UN) recognised Vesak as an international day in 1999. This means the festival is noticed worldwide.
64568.m: The UN has recognised Vesak since 1999.

64569.q: What do many Buddhists give at Vesak?
64569.e: At Vesak many people share food and drinks with others. They want to do good deeds.
64569.m: At Vesak many Buddhists share food with others.

64570.q: Which lanterns hang in South Korea for Buddha's birthday?
64570.e: In South Korea many lanterns shaped like lotus flowers hang up for Buddha's birthday. There are even big parades with them.
64570.m: In South Korea lotus lanterns shine for Buddha's birthday.

64571.q: According to Buddha's teaching, how should you treat animals?
64571.e: Buddha taught that you should treat all living beings kindly. Animals should not suffer either.
64571.m: Buddhists want to be kind to all living beings.

64572.q: What is the first rule for Buddhists?
a: Do not kill any living being
64572.e: The first of the rules says: do not kill or harm any living being. It applies to people and animals.
64572.m: The first rule is not to kill any living being.

64573.q: According to a story, which animal did the young Siddhartha save?
64573.e: His cousin shot a swan with an arrow. Siddhartha nursed the injured bird back to health.
64573.m: As a child Siddhartha saved an injured swan.

64574.e: “Metta” means loving kindness or friendliness. You wish all beings well.

64575.q: What do you wish all living beings in metta meditation?
64575.e: In metta meditation you think quietly: may all beings be happy. This makes your heart kind.
64575.m: In metta meditation you wish all beings happiness.

64576.q: What do many Buddhist monks eat to spare animals?
64576.e: Many Buddhists do not eat meat. That way no animal has to die for their food.
64576.m: Many Buddhists eat vegetarian food to spare animals.

64577.q: What do you call it when you feel that someone is sad and want to help them?
64577.e: Compassion is very important in Buddhism. You want others not to have to suffer.
64577.m: Compassion means feeling with others and helping.

64578.q: According to Buddha, who else should you treat kindly?
64578.e: Buddha taught that kindness applies to everyone, even to people who do not like us. Hatred is only ended by love.
64578.m: According to Buddha, kindness applies to all people.

64579.q: What is a large Japanese temple bell struck with?
64579.e: Japanese temple bells have no clapper inside. They are struck from the outside with a thick wooden beam.
64579.m: Large Japanese temple bells are struck with a wooden beam.

64580.q: How many times is the temple bell rung in Japan on New Year's Eve?
64580.e: In Japan the bell is struck 108 times on New Year's Eve. Each strike is meant to drive away a bad desire.
64580.m: In Japan the temple bell rings 108 times on New Year's Eve.

64581.q: What do temple bells call the monks to?
64581.e: The sound of the bell tells the monks when it is time for prayer and meditation. This is how the day begins in the monastery.
64581.m: Temple bells call the monks to meditate.

64582.q: What is a metal bowl that rings for a long time when struck called?
64582.e: A singing bowl is a bowl made of metal. When you strike it, it rings long and calmly.
64582.m: A singing bowl rings long and calmly.

64583.q: What often hangs from the corners of pagoda roofs?
64583.e: Small bells hang from the roof corners of many pagodas. The wind makes them ring.
64583.m: Small bells on pagodas ring in the wind.

64584.q: What is the sound of a temple bell meant to bring to the heart?
64584.e: The deep, long sound of the bell is meant to calm people. You listen to it until it fades away.
64584.m: The sound of the temple bell is meant to bring calm.

64585.q: What do Tibetan monks often hold together with a small hand bell?
64585.e: Tibetan monks hold the bell in their left hand and a small thunderbolt (dorje) in their right. The two belong together.
64585.m: The Tibetan hand bell goes with the thunderbolt.

64586.q: What is struck together with the small tingsha cymbals?
64586.e: Tingsha are two small metal discs on a cord. You strike them lightly together and hear a bright sound.
64586.m: With tingsha two small metal discs ring together.

64587.q: Which religion did Guru Nanak found?
64587.e: Guru Nanak is the first guru of the Sikhs. He founded Sikhism.
64587.m: Guru Nanak is the founder of Sikhism.

64588.q: In which present-day country is Guru Nanak's birthplace?
64588.e: Guru Nanak was born in Talwandi. Today the place is called Nankana Sahib and lies in Pakistan.
64588.m: Guru Nanak's birthplace is in Pakistan today.

64589.q: In which century was Guru Nanak born?
64589.e: Guru Nanak was born in 1469. That is in the 15th century.

64590.q: How many human gurus did the Sikhs have?
64590.e: Guru Nanak was followed by nine more gurus. Together there are ten human gurus.
64590.m: The Sikhs had ten human gurus.

64591.e: “Sikh” comes from a word meaning “to learn”. So a Sikh is a disciple or learner.
64591.m: A Sikh is a disciple who learns from the gurus.

64592.q: What did Guru Nanak teach about people?
64592.e: Guru Nanak taught that all people are of equal worth. Background and wealth should not matter.
64592.m: For Guru Nanak all people were of equal worth.

64593.q: How many gods did Guru Nanak believe in?
64593.e: Guru Nanak taught that there is only one God. This is an important foundation of Sikhism.
64593.m: Sikhs believe in one single God.

64594.q: What is the holy book of the Sikhs called?
64594.e: The holy book of the Sikhs is called the Guru Granth Sahib. It also contains hymns by Guru Nanak.
64594.m: The holy book of the Sikhs is the Guru Granth Sahib.

64595.q: What do many Sikh men wear on their heads?
64595.e: Many Sikhs wear a turban. In Punjabi it is called a dastar.
64595.m: Many Sikh men wear a turban.

64596.q: What does the Sikh turban cover?
64596.e: The turban protects the long hair. It keeps it clean and neatly together.
64596.m: The turban covers the uncut hair.

64597.q: What is a turban tied from?
64597.e: A turban is a long piece of cloth. It is wrapped around the head several times.
64597.m: A turban is a long, wrapped strip of cloth.

64598.q: What is the smaller head cloth that many Sikh boys wear instead of a turban called?
64598.e: Young boys often wear a patka. It is a simple cloth that holds the hair together.
64598.m: Many Sikh boys wear a patka.

64599.q: What do Sikhs often wear in their hair under the turban?
64599.e: The small wooden comb is called a kangha. It keeps the hair clean and tidy.
64599.m: The small Sikh comb is called a kangha.

64600.q: Which bangle do many Sikhs wear on their wrist?
64600.e: The bangle is called a kara and is usually made of steel or iron. It is a reminder of God, who has no beginning and no end.
64600.m: The Sikh steel bangle is called a kara.

64601.q: What do many devout Sikhs not cut?
64601.e: Uncut hair is called kesh. For many Sikhs it is a sign of their faith.
64601.m: Many Sikhs leave their hair uncut.

64602.q: In which city is the Golden Temple?
64602.e: The Golden Temple is in the city of Amritsar. Huge numbers of visitors go there every day.
64602.m: The Golden Temple is in Amritsar.

64603.e: Amritsar is in the state of Punjab in northern India. The Golden Temple stands there.

64604.q: For which religion is the Golden Temple most important?
64604.e: The Golden Temple is the most important holy place of the Sikhs. Many Sikhs would like to visit it once.
64604.m: The Golden Temple is the main holy place of the Sikhs.

64605.q: What is the Golden Temple surrounded by?
64605.e: The temple stands in the middle of a big pool of water. A walkway leads to the temple.
64605.m: The Golden Temple stands in a big pool of water.

64606.q: Why does the Golden Temple shine?
64606.e: The upper parts of the temple are covered in gold leaf. That is why it shines in the sun.
64606.m: The Golden Temple is covered in real gold.

64607.q: How many entrances does the Golden Temple have?
64607.e: The temple has four entrances, facing all four directions. This shows that everyone is welcome.
64607.m: The four entrances show that everyone is welcome.

64608.q: What must visitors cover in the Golden Temple?
64608.e: In the Golden Temple all visitors cover their heads. Shoes are taken off beforehand.
64608.m: In the Golden Temple you cover your head.

64609.q: What is the Golden Temple called in Punjabi?
64609.e: Its real name is Harmandir Sahib. This means something like “House of God”.
64609.m: The Golden Temple is called Harmandir Sahib.

64610.e: At the langar all visitors get a free meal. There is one in every Sikh temple.
64610.m: At the langar everyone eats together for free.

64611.q: Who can eat at the langar?
64611.e: Every guest is welcome at the langar. Religion, background and wealth do not matter.
64611.m: Everyone is welcome at the langar.

64612.q: How do people usually sit at the langar?
64612.e: At the langar everyone sits side by side in rows on the floor. That way nobody is higher than the others.
64612.m: At the langar everyone sits equally on the floor.

64613.q: What kind of food is served at the langar?
64613.e: The food at the langar is vegetarian. This means people of all religions can eat it.
64613.m: The food at the langar is vegetarian.

64614.q: Who cooks and serves at the langar?
64614.e: Volunteers cook, serve and wash up. This service for others is called seva.

64615.e: Even Guru Nanak had food cooked for everyone. This became the langar.
64615.m: The langar goes back to Guru Nanak.

64616.q: Which flatbread is often served at the langar?
64616.e: Roti is a thin flatbread from India. It is often served with lentils called dal.
64616.m: At the langar there is often roti and dal.

64617.q: What is a Sikh temple with a langar called?
64617.e: A Sikh temple is called a gurdwara. Every gurdwara has a kitchen for the langar.
64617.m: A Sikh temple is called a gurdwara.

64618.q: In which municipality in the canton of Bern is there a large Sikh temple?
64618.e: In Langenthal in the canton of Bern there is a large gurdwara. There is a langar for everyone there too.
64618.m: In Langenthal there is a Sikh temple with a langar.

64619.q: What else is Chinese New Year called in China?
64619.e: In China the New Year is also called the Spring Festival. It is the most important festival of the year.
64619.m: Chinese New Year is also called the Spring Festival.

64620.q: In which months does Chinese New Year fall?
64620.e: The festival is on a different day every year. But it is always between 21 January and 20 February.
64620.m: Chinese New Year is in January or February.

64621.q: Which colour is especially important at Chinese New Year?
64621.e: In China red is seen as the colour of luck. That is why lots of things are decorated in red for New Year.
64621.m: Red is the colour of luck in China.

64622.q: What do many families do before Chinese New Year?
64622.e: Before the festival the house is cleaned thoroughly. This sweeps out the bad luck of the old year.
64622.m: Before New Year the house is cleaned.

64623.q: Which animal is linked with the year 2026?
64623.e: The Year of the Horse began on 17 February 2026. Each year belongs to an animal.
64623.m: 2026 is the Year of the Horse.

64624.q: Many families eat filled dumplings at Chinese New Year. What does their shape remind people of?
64624.e: The dumplings are called jiaozi. Their shape is like old Chinese money and is meant to bring wealth.
64624.m: Chinese New Year dumplings look like old coins.

64625.q: Which festival ends the New Year celebrations after 15 days?
64625.e: On the 15th day of the new year the Lantern Festival is celebrated. Glowing lanterns hang everywhere.
64625.m: The Lantern Festival ends the New Year celebrations.

64626.q: What decides the date of Chinese New Year?
64626.e: The Chinese calendar follows the moon. That is why New Year is on a different day each year.
64626.m: Chinese New Year follows the moon.

64627.q: How many people carry a dragon in the dragon dance?
64627.e: The long dragon is carried by many dancers. Each holds a pole and moves one part of the dragon.
64627.m: In the dragon dance many dancers carry the dragon.

64628.q: What do the dancers hold the dragon up with?
64628.e: Poles are fixed underneath the dragon. The dancers use them to lift and swing the dragon.
64628.m: The dancers move the dragon with poles.

64629.q: What does the dragon stand for in China?
64629.e: In China the dragon is not a villain. It stands for luck, strength and wisdom.

64630.q: What does the dragon often chase in the dragon dance?
64630.e: A dancer at the front carries a ball on a pole. The dragon follows this “pearl” and twists back and forth.
64630.m: In the dance the dragon follows a ball.

64631.q: Which music goes with the dragon dance?
64631.e: Loud drums, cymbals and gongs set the beat. The noise is also meant to drive away evil spirits.
64631.m: Drums and cymbals go with the dragon dance.

64632.q: When do you often see a dragon dance in China?
64632.e: The dragon dance belongs especially to Chinese New Year. It is meant to bring luck for the new year.
64632.m: At Chinese New Year you often see dragon dances.

64633.q: What does an especially long dragon mean in the dance?
64633.e: People say: the longer the dragon, the more luck it brings. Some dragons are very long.
64633.m: A long dragon is meant to bring lots of luck.

64634.q: How many animals are there in the Chinese zodiac?
64634.e: The Chinese zodiac has twelve animals. Each year belongs to one of these animals.
64634.m: The Chinese zodiac has twelve animals.

64635.q: Which animal comes first in the Chinese zodiac?
64635.e: The rat is the first animal. According to legend, it won a race with a trick.
64635.m: The rat is the first animal in the zodiac.

64636.q: Which animal comes last in the Chinese zodiac?
64636.e: The pig is the twelfth and last animal. Before it come the dog and the rooster.
64636.m: The pig is the last animal in the zodiac.

64637.q: In the legend, which animal did the rat ride across the river?
64637.e: The clever rat sat on the ox's back. Just before the finish it jumped off and arrived first.
64637.m: The rat rode on the ox and won.

64638.q: Which animal is missing from the Chinese zodiac?
64638.e: The cat is not included. According to one legend, the rat did not wake it and it missed the race.
64638.m: The cat is not part of the Chinese zodiac.

64639.q: Which animal in the Chinese zodiac is a mythical creature?
64639.e: All the animals really exist except the dragon. It is a mythical creature.
64639.m: The dragon is the only mythical animal in the zodiac.

64640.q: Which animal comes straight after the dragon in the Chinese zodiac?
64640.e: The dragon is followed by the snake. After that comes the horse.
64640.m: After the dragon comes the snake.

64641.q: Which animal comes straight after the tiger in the Chinese zodiac?
64641.e: The order begins with rat, ox, tiger and rabbit. So after the tiger comes the rabbit.
64641.m: After the tiger comes the rabbit.

64642.q: Which two colours does the yin and yang symbol have?
64642.e: The symbol has a black half and a white half. The halves curve like drops.
64642.m: The yin and yang symbol is black and white.

64643.q: Which country does the idea of yin and yang come from?
64643.e: Yin and yang is an old idea from China. It is very important in Taoism.
64643.m: Yin and yang comes from China.

64644.q: What is in each half of the yin and yang symbol?
a: A dot of the other colour
64644.e: In the black half there is a white dot and the other way round. Each contains a little of the other.
64644.m: Each half has a dot of the other colour.

64645.q: What shape is the yin and yang symbol?
64645.e: The symbol is a circle. A curved line divides it into two halves.
64645.m: The yin and yang symbol is a circle.

64646.q: What does the yin and yang symbol show?
64646.e: Yin and yang are opposites like light and dark. They belong together and complete each other.
64646.m: Yin and yang shows that opposites belong together.

64647.e: Yang is the bright, warm side. It is often linked with the sun.
64647.m: Yang stands for light and warmth.

64648.q: Which pair goes well with yin and yang?
64648.e: Day and night are opposites that take turns. Yin and yang complete each other in just the same way.
64648.m: Day and night are like yin and yang.

64649.q: How do you politely hand over a red lucky envelope in China?
64649.e: You give and take the red envelope with both hands. This shows respect.
64649.m: You hand over a hongbao with both hands.

64650.q: What is inside a red lucky envelope?
64650.e: The red envelopes contain money. It is meant to bring luck for the new year.

64651.q: Who usually gets a red lucky envelope?
64651.e: Older relatives give the children red envelopes. In return the children wish them a happy new year.
64651.m: Children get red envelopes at New Year.

64652.q: What are the red lucky envelopes called in Chinese?
64652.e: Hongbao means “red packet”. In some areas they are also called lai see.
64652.m: The red lucky envelopes are called hongbao.

64653.q: Which number is seen as lucky in China?
64653.e: In Chinese, eight sounds similar to “getting rich”. That is why it is seen as a lucky number.
64653.m: In China eight is a lucky number.

64654.q: Which number do people avoid for gifts of money in China?
64654.e: In Chinese, four sounds similar to the word for “death”. That is why people do not give amounts with a four.
64654.m: In China four is seen as an unlucky number.

64655.q: How are many hongbao sent in China today?
64655.e: Today many people send digital red envelopes. This is done with apps on their phones.
64655.m: Today hongbao also come digitally on phones.

64656.q: Which country does the Shinto religion come from?
64656.e: Shinto is the old religion of Japan. There are very many Shinto shrines in Japan.
64656.m: Shinto is the old religion of Japan.

64657.q: What are the gods and spirits in Shinto called?
64657.e: In Shinto the beings that are worshipped are called kami. They live, for example, in mountains, trees or rivers.
64657.m: In Shinto the gods are called kami.

64658.q: What do you do with water first at a Shinto shrine?
64658.e: At the water basin you rinse your hands and mouth. This is how you purify yourself before praying.
64658.m: Before praying you clean your hands and mouth.

64659.q: How many times do you usually clap when praying at a Shinto shrine?
64659.e: You bow twice, clap twice and bow once more. This is how you greet the kami.
64659.m: When praying at the shrine you clap twice.

64660.q: What are omikuji at a Shinto shrine?
64660.e: Omikuji are small slips that foretell good or bad luck. Bad ones are often tied up at the shrine.

64661.q: What do you write on a small wooden plaque at the shrine?
64661.e: The wooden plaques are called ema. People write wishes on them and hang them up at the shrine.
64661.m: You write a wish on an ema.

64662.q: Which animal is often seen as a statue at Inari shrines?
64662.e: Foxes are seen as messengers of the god Inari. That is why there are many fox statues at Inari shrines.
64662.m: There are fox statues at Inari shrines.

64663.q: What does the word Shinto mean?
64663.e: Translated, Shinto means “way of the gods”. The word is made up of two characters.

a: A gate in front of a shrine
64664.e: A torii is a large gate. It stands at the entrance to a Shinto shrine.
64664.m: A torii is the gate to a Shinto shrine.

64665.q: In which country are there the most torii?
64665.e: Torii belong to Shinto shrines. That is why almost all torii are in Japan.
64665.m: Torii are mainly found in Japan.

64666.e: Many torii are painted bright orange-red. The colour is meant to keep bad luck away.

64667.q: What are most torii made of?
64667.e: Most torii are made of wood. But there are also torii made of stone or metal.
64667.m: Most torii are made of wood.

64668.q: How many posts does a torii usually have?
64668.e: A torii has two upright posts. Two crossbeams lie across the top.
64668.m: A torii usually has two posts.

64669.q: Where does the famous torii of Miyajima stand?
64669.e: The great torii of the Itsukushima Shrine stands in the sea. At high tide it seems to float on the water.
64669.m: The torii of Miyajima stands in the sea.

64670.q: What do the thousands of torii at the Fushimi Inari Shrine in Kyoto form?
64670.e: At the Fushimi Inari Shrine thousands of torii stand close together one after another. They form long tunnels up the mountain.
64670.m: The Fushimi Inari Shrine has thousands of torii.

64671.q: What do people in Japan admire during Hanami?
64671.e: During Hanami people admire the cherry trees in blossom. All over Japan people look forward to it.
64671.m: During Hanami people admire the cherry blossom.

64672.q: In which season is the cherry blossom festival?
64672.e: The cherry trees blossom in spring. In Tokyo this is usually at the end of March or the start of April.
64672.m: The cherry blossom festival is in spring.

64673.q: What is cherry blossom called in Japanese?
64673.e: The Japanese word for cherry blossom is sakura. It is a very popular flower in Japan.
64673.m: Cherry blossom is called sakura in Japanese.

64674.q: What do many families do during Hanami?
a: Have a picnic under the trees
64674.e: People sit on blankets under the trees in blossom. There they eat and celebrate together.
64674.m: During Hanami people have picnics under cherry trees.

64675.q: What does the word Hanami mean?
64675.e: Hana means flower and mi means looking. So Hanami means looking at blossoms.

64676.q: What colour is cherry blossom usually?
64676.e: Most cherry blossom is pale pink or white. Whole parks then glow brightly.
64676.m: Cherry blossom is usually pink or white.

64677.q: Roughly how long do the cherry trees blossom?
64677.e: The cherry blossom lasts only a short time, about one to two weeks. That is why everyone looks forward to it so much.
64677.m: The cherry blossom lasts only about one to two weeks.

64678.q: Where in Japan do the cherry trees blossom last?
a: Only on islands in the south
64678.e: In the warm south the cherry trees blossom first. In the cold north, on Hokkaido, they only blossom in May.
64678.m: In the cold north of Japan the cherries blossom last.

64679.q: What do people eat at the Chinese Moon Festival?
64679.e: For the Moon Festival people bake mooncakes. They are often filled with sweet paste.
64679.m: At the Moon Festival people eat mooncakes.

64680.e: Mooncakes are round like the full moon. The round shape stands for the family coming together.
64680.m: Mooncakes are round like the full moon.

64681.q: In which season is the Moon Festival celebrated?
64681.e: The Moon Festival is also called the Mid-Autumn Festival. It is usually in September or early October.
64681.m: The Moon Festival is celebrated in autumn.

64682.q: What does the moon look like at the Moon Festival?
64682.e: The Moon Festival is on the 15th day of the eighth lunar month. Then there is a full moon and the moon is especially bright.
64682.m: At the Moon Festival there is a full moon.

64683.q: What is the moon goddess in the Chinese legend called?
64683.e: According to the legend, the goddess Chang'e lives on the moon. Her story is told at the Moon Festival.
64683.m: The Chinese moon goddess is called Chang'e.

64684.q: In the legend, which animal lives on the moon with the moon goddess?
64684.e: A white jade rabbit keeps the moon goddess company. According to the legend, it pounds a medicine.
64684.m: The jade rabbit lives on the moon.

64685.q: Who do people mainly celebrate the Moon Festival with?
64685.e: At the Moon Festival families come together. They look at the moon together and eat mooncakes.
64685.m: The Moon Festival is celebrated with the family.

64686.q: What do children often carry around at the Moon Festival?
64686.e: Children carry colourful lanterns in lots of shapes. The lights glow in the dark.
64686.m: At the Moon Festival children carry lanterns.

64687.q: What is a totem pole usually made from?
64687.e: Totem poles are carved from big tree trunks. The wood of the western red cedar is often used.
64687.m: A totem pole is carved from a tree trunk.

64688.q: On which continent are the well-known totem poles?
64688.e: The peoples of the north-west coast of North America carve totem poles, for example in Canada and Alaska.
64688.m: Totem poles come from the north-west coast of North America.

64689.q: What is often carved on a totem pole?
64689.e: Animals such as the bear, beaver, wolf or whale are carved on totem poles. They stand for families and their stories.
64689.m: You can see lots of animals on totem poles.

64690.q: What does a totem pole tell?
a: The number of fish in the sea
64690.e: A totem pole tells the history and origins of a family or clan. Each figure has a meaning.
64690.m: A totem pole is like a storybook made of wood.

64691.q: Which bird is especially common on totem poles?
64691.e: The raven is an important figure for the peoples of the north-west coast. In many stories it brings light to people.
64691.m: The raven plays a big part in the stories of the north-west coast.

64692.q: Are totem poles worshipped as gods?
a: Yes, as the village's protecting gods
64692.e: Totem poles are not images of gods. They show family crest animals and remember families, ancestors and important events.
64692.m: Totem poles are not worshipped; they remember families.

64693.q: How do totem poles usually stand?
64693.e: Totem poles are set upright in the ground. Many stand in front of houses or villages.
64693.m: A totem pole stands upright like a tree.

64694.q: Which people is known for its totem poles?
64694.e: The Haida live on the coast of Canada and Alaska. They are famous carvers of totem poles.
64694.m: The Haida carve famous totem poles.

64695.q: What can totem poles look like?
64695.e: Many totem poles are painted, for example in red, black and blue-green. This makes the figures stand out well.
64695.m: Many totem poles are painted in colours.

64696.q: Which people do the stories of the Dreamtime belong to?
64696.e: The Dreamtime belongs to the beliefs of the Aboriginal peoples. Its stories tell how the world came to be.
64696.m: The Dreamtime is the belief of the Aboriginal peoples.

64697.q: In which country do the Aboriginal peoples live?
64697.e: The Aboriginal peoples are the original inhabitants of Australia. They have lived there for many tens of thousands of years.
64697.m: The Aboriginal peoples are Australia's first people.

64698.q: According to the Aboriginal peoples, what happened in the Dreamtime?
64698.e: In the Dreamtime ancestral beings shaped the land, the animals and the plants. They also gave people rules for living.
64698.m: In the Dreamtime the world was created.

64699.q: Which big creature is an important being of the Dreamtime?
64699.e: The Rainbow Serpent is a powerful ancestral being. It is said to have shaped rivers and waterholes.
64699.m: According to the belief, the Rainbow Serpent shaped rivers and waterholes.

64700.q: What do Aboriginal artists often paint their pictures with?
64700.e: Dot painting is typical for many Aboriginal artists. The pictures tell stories from the Dreamtime.
64700.m: Many Aboriginal pictures are made of dots.

64701.q: Which musical instrument comes from the Aboriginal peoples?
64701.e: The didgeridoo is a long wind instrument made from a branch hollowed out by termites. It sounds deep and droning.
64701.m: The didgeridoo is an Aboriginal instrument.

64702.q: How do the Aboriginal peoples pass on the stories of the Dreamtime?
64702.e: The stories have been passed on by word of mouth for a very long time. Songs, dances and pictures help people remember.
64702.m: The Dreamtime is passed on through songs and stories.

64703.q: What are the sung paths across the land of the Aboriginal peoples called?
64703.e: Songlines, or dreaming tracks, are the paths of the ancestral beings. With songs, people could remember the way across the land.
64703.m: Songlines are paths that are learned through songs.

64704.q: What is sacred to the Aboriginal peoples?
64704.e: For the Aboriginal peoples the land is sacred. Every mountain, river and rock has a story from the Dreamtime.
64704.m: For the Aboriginal peoples the land has a sacred meaning.

64705.e: Uluru is in the Northern Territory, almost in the middle of the country. It is one of the best-known landmarks there.
64705.m: Uluru is in the middle of Australia.

64706.e: Uluru is an enormous sandstone rock. It is several kilometres long.

64707.e: Uluru glows reddish. At sunrise and sunset it looks especially deep red.
64707.m: Uluru glows red in the evening sun.

64708.q: What was Uluru called in English in the past?
64708.e: In 1873 an explorer named the rock after a politician called Henry Ayers. Today the Aboriginal name is used again.
64708.m: Uluru used to be called Ayers Rock.

64709.q: For whom is Uluru a sacred place?
64709.e: The Aboriginal peoples are Australia's first people. For the Anangu, who live around Uluru, the rock is sacred.
64709.m: Uluru is sacred to the Aboriginal peoples.

64710.q: What have visitors not been allowed to do at Uluru since 2019?
64710.e: Since October 2019 climbing Uluru has been banned. This respects the Anangu's sacred place.
64710.m: You may no longer climb Uluru.

64711.q: Roughly how high does Uluru rise above the plain?
64711.e: Uluru rises about 348 metres above the flat land around it. That is higher than the Eiffel Tower.

64712.q: What is the landscape like around Uluru?
64712.e: Uluru lies in a hot, dry area in the interior of Australia. All around, the land is wide and flat.
64712.m: Around Uluru the land is dry and flat.

64713.q: Which instrument does a shaman use especially often?
64713.e: Shamans beat a drum in a steady rhythm. This is meant to help them make contact with the spirit world.
64713.m: The drum is the shaman's most important instrument.

a: A healer who is said to talk to spirits
64714.e: A shaman is seen as a healer by his people. People believe that he can speak with spirits.
64714.m: A shaman is a healer who is said to speak with spirits.

64715.q: Where does the word ‘shaman’ come from?
64715.e: The word comes from the language of a people in Siberia. Later it was used for similar healers all over the world.
64715.m: The word shaman comes from Siberia.

64716.q: What is the skin of a shaman's drum often made of?
64716.e: An animal hide is stretched over a wooden frame. In Siberia and the far north this is often reindeer hide.
64716.m: A shaman's drum has a skin made of animal hide.

64717.q: According to the belief, in what form do a shaman's helping spirits often appear?
64717.e: Many shamans believe in helping spirits. These often appear as animals, for example as a bear, a bird or a wolf.
64717.m: Shamans' helping spirits often take the form of animals.

64718.q: Which people in northern Europe had shamans with magic drums?
64718.e: The Sami live in Lapland in northern Europe. Their shamans were called noaidi and used a drum.
64718.m: The Sami in Lapland had shamans too.

64719.q: What shape is a shaman's drum often?
64719.e: Most shaman drums are round. You hold them in one hand and beat them with a beater.
64719.m: A shaman's drum is usually round.

64720.q: What do the pictures on some shaman drums show?
64720.e: Many drums have animals, the sun, the moon and spirits painted on them. They show how the people imagined the world.
64720.m: Shaman drums often have animals and spirits painted on them.

a: Many Indigenous peoples of North America
64721.e: Many Indigenous peoples of North America believe in a great power that created everything. It is often called the Great Spirit.
64721.m: Many Indigenous peoples of North America believe in the Great Spirit.

64722.q: Where do many Indigenous peoples of North America feel the Great Spirit?
64722.e: For many Indigenous peoples the Great Spirit is in everything: in animals, plants, mountains and the wind. That is why they respect nature.
64722.m: The Great Spirit is in all of nature.

64723.q: What do some peoples in north-eastern America call the Great Spirit?
64723.e: Among the Algonquian peoples the Great Spirit is called Manitou or Gitche Manitou. It means a power that is in everything.
64723.m: Manitou is a name for the Great Spirit.

64724.q: What do many Indigenous peoples of North America call the earth?
64724.e: Many Indigenous peoples call the earth “Mother Earth”. It gives food and life and is therefore respected.
64724.m: Many Indigenous peoples call the earth Mother.

64725.q: Which feather is seen as sacred by many Indigenous peoples of North America?
64725.e: The eagle flies very high and is seen as a messenger to the sky. That is why its feathers are very precious.
64725.m: The eagle feather is sacred to many Indigenous peoples.

64726.q: What is a dreamcatcher meant to catch?
64726.e: The dreamcatcher comes from the Ojibwe. According to the belief, bad dreams get caught in the net while good dreams slide down to the sleeper.
64726.m: A dreamcatcher is meant to catch bad dreams.

64727.q: Which animal was especially important for the peoples of the prairie?
64727.e: The bison gave meat, hide and bones for tools. That is why it was honoured and thanked.
64727.m: The bison was very important for the prairie peoples.

64728.q: What is passed round in a circle at ceremonies of some Indigenous peoples of North America?
64728.e: At important meetings a sacred pipe was passed round in a circle. The smoke was meant to carry prayers to the Great Spirit.
64728.m: The sacred pipe links people with the Great Spirit.

64729.q: What is the famous war dance of the Maori called?
64729.e: The haka is a powerful dance with shouting, stamping and faces. New Zealand's rugby team performs it before matches.
64729.m: The haka is the famous dance of the Maori.

64731.q: Who does the carved Maori meeting house represent?
64731.e: The meeting house represents the body of an ancestor. The ridge beam is the backbone and the rafters are the ribs.
64731.m: The Maori meeting house is built like an ancestor.

64732.q: What do some Maori wear on their faces as a sign of their family?
64732.e: The tattoo called ta moko shows a person's origins and family. Every line has a meaning.
64732.m: Ta moko is the Maori tattoo.

64733.q: What do the Maori carve their precious pendants from?
64733.e: The green stone is called pounamu, a kind of jade. Pendants made from it are often handed down in the family.

64734.q: Why are ancestors so important to the Maori?
64734.e: The Maori often know the names of their ancestors over many generations. When introducing themselves, people name their canoe, their mountain and their tribe.
64734.m: The Maori feel closely connected to their ancestors.

64735.q: When is the midsummer bonfire lit?
64735.e: Around 21 June is the summer solstice. On this day the sun is at its highest.
64735.m: The midsummer bonfire burns around 21 June.

64736.q: What is special about the day of the summer solstice?
64736.e: At the summer solstice the sun shines for longest here. After that the days get shorter again.
64736.m: The summer solstice is the longest day of the year.

64737.q: What is the shortest day of the year?
64737.e: The winter solstice is around 21 December. Then the day is shortest and the night is longest.
64737.m: At the winter solstice the night is longest.

64738.q: What do people celebrate with the solstice bonfire?
64738.e: Since ancient times people have honoured the power of the sun with fire. The fire stands for light and warmth.
64738.m: The solstice bonfire celebrates the sun.

64739.q: Where are solstice bonfires often lit in the Alps?
64739.e: On mountains and hills the fires can be seen far down into the valley. In the Alps many fires glow on this night.
64739.m: Solstice bonfires like to burn on mountains.

64740.q: Which old custom belongs to the solstice bonfire?
64740.e: In the past young people jumped over the low fire. This was meant to bring luck and good health.
64740.m: In the past people jumped over the flames of the solstice bonfire.

64741.q: What is the fire around 24 June that is named after a saint called?
64741.e: 24 June is St John's Day. St John's fire is related to the old solstice bonfire.
64741.m: St John's fire burns around 24 June.

64742.q: How many solstices are there in a year?
64742.e: There is one solstice in summer and one in winter. In between come the equinoxes in spring and autumn.
64742.m: Every year there are two solstices.

64743.q: What are the stones of Stonehenge lined up with?
64743.e: On the morning of the summer solstice the sun rises in line with the entrance. That is why many people come here on that day.
64743.m: Stonehenge is lined up with the sun.

64744.e: Stonehenge was built as early as the New Stone Age. The druids lived much later.
64744.m: Stonehenge is older than the druids.

64745.e: Stonehenge has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986. This is meant to protect it for all time.
64745.m: Stonehenge is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

64746.e: The druids were highly respected among the Celts. They led sacrifices and festivals.
64746.m: The druids were the priests of the Celts.

64747.q: Which tree was especially sacred to the druids?
64747.e: The Celts saw the oak as a sacred tree. The druids often held their rituals under oaks.
64747.m: The oak was sacred to the druids.

64748.q: Which Celtic tribe lived in the area of present-day Switzerland?
64748.e: The Helvetii were a Celtic tribe on the Swiss Plateau. The name Helvetia for Switzerland comes from them.
64748.m: The Helvetii were Celts in Switzerland.

64749.q: On which lake is the Celtic site of La Tène, after which a whole era is named?
64749.e: At La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel many Celtic weapons and pieces of jewellery were found. That is why a Celtic era is called the La Tène period.
64749.m: La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel gave its name to a Celtic era.

64750.q: Which famous Roman wrote about the druids?
64750.e: Julius Caesar described the Celts and their druids in his book about the Gallic War. Much of what we know comes from him.
64750.m: Julius Caesar wrote about the druids.

64751.q: Which Celtic festival is seen as the origin of Halloween?
64751.e: Samhain was celebrated at the end of October. The Celts believed that the world of spirits was especially close then.
64751.m: Halloween has its roots in the Celtic festival of Samhain.

64752.q: What did the druids do when the Celts quarrelled?
64752.e: The druids were also judges. They made decisions in disputes and their rulings were followed.

64753.e: Mistletoe grows as a round bush high up on the branches of trees. You can see it especially well in winter.

64754.e: Mistletoe has white, sticky berries. They are poisonous for people and must not be eaten.

64755.q: According to old reports, what did the Celtic druids cut mistletoe with?
64755.e: The Roman Pliny wrote that druids cut mistletoe with a golden sickle. It was seen as sacred.
64755.m: The druids cut mistletoe with a golden sickle.

64756.q: Who spreads the seeds of mistletoe?
64756.e: Birds eat the berries and wipe the sticky seeds off on branches. That is how a new mistletoe grows.
64756.m: Birds spread mistletoe from tree to tree.

64757.q: According to a custom, what do people do under a sprig of mistletoe at Christmas?
a: They give each other a kiss
64757.e: The custom is especially common in England. People who meet under the mistletoe may kiss.
64757.m: Under the mistletoe people give each other a kiss.

64758.q: What happens to mistletoe leaves in winter?
a: They turn yellow and fall off
64758.e: Mistletoe does not lose its leaves in winter. That is why it used to be seen as a sign of life.
64758.m: Mistletoe is green even in winter.

64759.e: Mistletoe has no roots in the ground. It taps into the tree and takes water and minerals from it.
64759.m: Mistletoe gets water from its tree.

64760.q: Which bird is named after mistletoe?
64760.e: The mistle thrush likes eating mistletoe berries. That is why it has this name.
64760.m: The mistle thrush likes eating mistletoe berries.

64761.e: Ancestors are your forebears: grandparents, great-grandparents and everyone before them. In many parts of Africa they are honoured.
64761.m: Ancestors are the forebears of a family.

64762.q: What do many people in Africa believe about their ancestors?
64762.e: According to this belief, the dead ancestors watch over their family. They can give advice and protection.
64762.m: In many parts of Africa ancestors are seen as protectors of the family.

64763.q: What are ancestors in Africa often given as gifts?
64763.e: The ancestors are given food and drink. Sometimes a little drink is poured on the ground for them.
64763.m: Ancestors are given food and drink.

64764.q: What are African ancestor figures often carved from?
64764.e: Many ancestor figures are carved from wood. They are reminders of family members who have died.
64764.m: African ancestor figures are often made of wood.

64765.q: In which country are there colourful coffins shaped like fish or cars?
64765.e: In Ghana craftspeople build coffins in many fun shapes. The shape is a reminder of the dead person's job or favourite things.
64765.m: In Ghana there are coffins in fantasy shapes.

64766.q: Why do many African families tell stories about their ancestors?
a: So that they are not forgotten
64766.e: As long as the ancestors are remembered, they belong to the family. That is why their names and stories are passed on.
64766.m: Through stories the ancestors are remembered.

64767.q: Who is one of your ancestors?
64767.e: Ancestors are the people who lived in your family before you, for example grandparents and great-grandparents. In many parts of Africa they are honoured as ancestors.

64768.q: According to African belief, who do people ask for advice when making important decisions?
64768.e: At important events such as a wedding or a birth, people call on the ancestors. They ask them for advice and blessing.
64768.m: At important events people ask the ancestors for a blessing.

64769.q: What are many African masks made of?
64769.e: African masks are usually carved from wood. They are often decorated with paint, shells or feathers.
64769.m: Many African masks are carved from wood.

64770.q: What do the masks at many old festivals often represent?
64770.e: According to old belief, whoever wears the mask turns into a spirit being. That is why the person behind it is often kept secret.
64770.m: With a mask you turn into a different being.

64771.q: What are the wild wooden masks from the Lötschental valley in Valais called?
64771.e: The Tschäggättä wear fierce wooden masks and sheep or goat skins. They roam through the villages at carnival time.
64771.m: The Tschäggättä come from the Lötschental.

64772.q: What are the masks at the Basel carnival called?
64772.e: At the Basel carnival the carnival-goers wear large masks called Larven. They are often made of papier-mâché.
64772.m: At the Basel carnival people wear Larven.

64773.q: Where do the Silvesterchläuse go from farm to farm with their bells?
64773.e: In the Appenzell region the Silvesterchläuse go from farm to farm and wish everyone a happy New Year. They come on New Year's Eve and on 13 January.
64773.m: The Silvesterchläuse go through the Appenzell region.

64774.q: In which African country do the Dogon people dance with tall wooden masks?
64774.e: The Dogon live in Mali. They dance with tall carved masks to honour the dead.
64774.m: The Dogon in Mali are known for their mask dances.

64775.q: In which city in Italy is the carnival with masks famous?
64775.e: At the carnival in Venice many people wear elaborate masks and costumes. It has been famous for centuries.
64775.m: The Venice carnival is famous for its masks.

64776.q: Why do people wear wild masks at some winter customs?
64776.e: According to old custom, loud, wild figures are meant to drive away the winter and evil spirits. That is why the masks are often frightening.
64776.m: Wild masks are meant to drive away the winter.

64777.q: What hangs around the bodies of the Silvesterchläuse?
64777.e: The Silvesterchläuse wear heavy bells. When they walk, the bells ring loudly through the village.

64778.q: What was the Egyptian god Ra in charge of?
64778.e: Ra (also Re) was the sun god in ancient Egypt. The Egyptians saw his power in the sun.
64778.m: Ra was the sun god of the ancient Egyptians.

64779.q: According to Egyptian belief, what did Ra travel across the sky in every day?
64779.e: The Egyptians believed that Ra travelled across the sky in a solar barque. A barque is a boat.
64779.m: Ra travelled across the sky in a solar barque.

64780.q: Which animal's head does Ra have in many Egyptian pictures?
64780.e: Ra is often shown as a man with the head of a falcon. On his head he wears a sun disc.
64780.m: In pictures Ra often has a falcon's head with a sun disc.

64781.q: What does Ra usually wear on his head in pictures?
64781.e: A round sun disc floats above his head. It is often surrounded by a snake.
64781.m: The sun disc on his head shows that Ra is the sun god.

64782.q: According to Egyptian belief, where did Ra travel at night?
64782.e: In the evening the sun went down. The Egyptians believed that Ra then travelled through the underworld and rose again in the morning.
64782.m: At night Ra travelled through the underworld.

64783.q: Which creature did Ra have to fight at night?
64783.e: The evil snake Apophis wanted to stop the solar barque. Ra and his helpers defeated it every night.
64783.m: Ra defeated the snake Apophis every night.

64784.q: As which animal did the Egyptians show the morning sun?
64784.e: The morning sun was called Khepri and was shown as a scarab. A scarab is a beetle that rolls a ball in front of it.
64784.m: The morning sun was shown as a scarab beetle.

64785.q: What did the pharaohs call themselves to show they were close to the sun god?
64785.e: The kings of Egypt bore the title “Son of Ra”. In this way they showed that they were connected to the sun god.
64785.m: A pharaoh called himself “Son of Ra”.

64786.q: Which animal's head does the Egyptian god Anubis have?
64786.e: Anubis is shown as a man with the head of a jackal. A jackal looks rather like a dog.
64786.m: Anubis has the head of a jackal.

64787.q: What was Anubis in charge of for the ancient Egyptians?
64787.e: Anubis was the god of the dead and of cemeteries. He protected the tombs.
64787.m: Anubis was the god of the dead and of tombs.

64788.q: According to Egyptian belief, which work did Anubis help with?
64788.e: Anubis was seen as the god of mummification. The priests who embalmed the dead sometimes wore an Anubis mask.
64788.m: Anubis helped with embalming the dead.

64789.q: What colour is Anubis usually in Egyptian pictures?
64789.e: Anubis is usually painted black. Black reminded people of the fertile soil by the Nile and of new life.
64789.m: In pictures Anubis is usually black.

64790.q: According to Egyptian belief, what did Anubis weigh at the judgement of the dead?
64790.e: The dead person's heart was placed on a pair of scales. On the other side lay a feather, which stood for truth.
64790.m: At the judgement of the dead the heart was weighed against a feather.

64791.q: Why was Anubis probably given a jackal's head?
64791.e: In Egypt jackals often wandered around the tombs at the edge of the desert. That is why the jackal became the animal of the god of the dead.
64791.m: Jackals roamed around the tombs, so the jackal became Anubis's animal.

64792.q: According to Egyptian belief, who did Anubis accompany?
64792.e: Anubis led the dead into the afterlife. He watched over them on the way.
64792.m: Anubis led the dead into the afterlife.

64793.q: According to Egyptian belief, what did Anubis watch over?
64793.e: Anubis was seen as the lord of the cities of the dead, that is, the large cemeteries. He was meant to protect the tombs from disturbance.

64794.q: Who was the goddess Isis for the ancient Egyptians?
64794.e: Isis was one of the most important goddesses of Egypt. She was seen as a loving mother and a protector.
64794.m: Isis was the great mother goddess of Egypt.

64795.q: What was the name of the goddess Isis's husband?
64795.e: Isis was married to the god Osiris. Osiris later became the ruler of the realm of the dead.
64795.m: Isis was the wife of Osiris.

64796.q: What was the name of Isis's son with the falcon's head?
64796.e: Horus was the son of Isis and Osiris. He is often shown with the head of a falcon.
64796.m: Horus was the son of Isis.

64797.q: What does Isis often wear on her head in old pictures?
64797.e: Isis often wears the sign for a throne on her head. Her name also means “throne” or “seat”.
64797.m: Isis wears a throne as a sign on her head.

64798.q: According to the legend, what did Isis do when her husband was killed?
64798.e: The evil Seth killed Osiris and scattered his body. Isis searched for all the pieces and brought Osiris back to life with magic.
64798.m: Isis brought her husband back to life with magic.
