65153.m: Jesus spoke to Saul near Damascus.

65154.q: For how many days could Saul not see anything afterwards?
65154.e: Saul was blind for three days. During this time he ate and drank nothing.
65154.m: Saul was blind for three days.

65155.q: Who laid his hands on Saul so that he could see again?
65155.e: God sent a disciple called Ananias to Saul. When he laid his hands on him, Saul could see again.
65155.m: Ananias helped Saul to see again.

65156.q: Which saying comes from the story of Saul?
a: “I can't see the wood for the trees”
65156.e: When Saul could see again, something like scales fell from his eyes. Today people say this when they suddenly understand something.
65156.m: When you suddenly understand something, the scales fall from your eyes.

65157.q: How did Paul later escape from the city of Damascus?
a: In a basket over the wall
65157.e: Enemies were guarding the city gates. So friends lowered him down over the city wall in a basket at night.
65157.m: Paul escaped from Damascus in a basket.

65158.q: On which day after Easter do Christians celebrate Ascension?
65158.e: Ascension is 40 days after Easter if you count Easter Sunday. Christians remember that Jesus ascended into heaven.
65158.m: Ascension is celebrated 40 days after Easter.

65159.q: What do Christians celebrate at Pentecost?
65159.e: At Pentecost Christians remember that the Holy Spirit came to the disciples of Jesus. Pentecost is 50 days after Easter.
65159.m: At Pentecost Christians celebrate the Holy Spirit.

65160.q: What is the great Muslim festival called at which families share meat with poor people?
65160.e: The Festival of Sacrifice is the most important festival in Islam. It remembers Abraham, who trusted God completely. Food is shared with family, friends and the poor.
65160.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is the biggest festival in Islam.

65161.q: Where do many Catholic families go on All Saints' Day?
65161.e: All Saints' Day is on 1 November. Many families then visit the graves of their loved ones who have died and decorate them.
65161.m: On All Saints' Day many people visit the graves.

65162.q: How many times a day do devout Muslims pray?
65162.e: The obligatory prayer in Islam is said five times a day. It is spread from early morning into the night.
65162.m: Devout Muslims pray five times a day.

65163.q: What do many Muslims kneel on when they pray?
65163.e: Prayer takes place in a clean spot. That is why many Muslims lay out their own prayer rug.
65163.m: Muslims often pray on a prayer rug.

65164.q: What do Muslims do before prayer?
65164.e: Before prayer Muslims wash their hands, face, arms and feet. This washing is called wudu.

65165.q: How do many Christians hold their hands when praying?
65165.e: Many Christians fold their hands to pray. In this way they show that they are becoming calm and thinking of God.
65165.m: Many Christians fold their hands when they pray.

65166.q: Which word do Christians say at the end of a prayer?
65166.e: Amen is a Hebrew word. It means “so be it”.
65166.m: At the end of a prayer you say Amen.

65167.q: What is the prayer chain of Catholic Christians called?
65167.e: With the rosary you move one bead along for each prayer. That way you know how many prayers you have already said.
65167.m: The Catholic prayer chain is called the rosary.

65168.q: What is food that is allowed according to Jewish rules called?
65168.e: Kosher means “fit” or “suitable”. The Jewish food rules say what you may eat.
65168.m: Food allowed in Judaism is called kosher.

65169.q: What is food that is allowed according to Islamic rules called?
65169.e: Halal is an Arabic word and means “allowed”. What is forbidden is called haram.
65169.m: Food allowed in Islam is called halal.

65170.q: Which meat do devout Jews and Muslims not eat?
65170.e: In Judaism and Islam the pig is considered unclean. That is why devout people do not eat pork.
65170.m: Devout Jews and Muslims do not eat pork.

65171.q: What may devout Jews not eat together?
65171.e: According to the Jewish food rules, meat and milk are kept apart. Many families even have separate crockery for them.
65171.m: In Judaism meat and milk are not eaten together.

65172.q: Which drink is forbidden for devout Muslims?
65172.e: The Quran forbids intoxicating drinks. That is why devout Muslims do not drink alcohol.
65172.m: Devout Muslims do not drink alcohol.

65173.q: What do men put on their heads when they visit a synagogue?
65173.e: In the synagogue Jewish men cover their heads when they pray. Visitors are also given a kippah there.
65173.m: In the synagogue men cover their heads.

65174.q: What is the cube-shaped building in Mecca called?
65174.e: The Kaaba is the most important holy site in Islam. It is covered with a black cloth.
65174.m: The holy site in Mecca is called the Kaaba.

65175.q: What do visitors put into the cracks of the Western Wall?
65175.e: The Western Wall in Jerusalem is part of the wall around the ancient Jewish Temple. Many people write prayers and wishes on notes and push them between the stones.
65175.m: People put notes with prayers into the Western Wall.

65176.q: How many times a day do the bells ring for the Angelus in many Catholic places?
65176.e: The Angelus bell rings in the morning, at midday and in the evening. It invites people to say a short prayer.
65176.m: The bells ring for the Angelus three times a day.

65177.q: What is the muezzin's call to prayer called?
65177.e: With the adhan the muezzin calls Muslims to prayer. The call can be heard several times a day.
65177.m: The call to prayer in Islam is called the adhan.

65178.q: In which language does the muezzin call people to prayer?
65178.e: The call to prayer is made in Arabic all over the world. That is also the language of the Quran.
65178.m: The muezzin calls to prayer in Arabic.

65179.q: The shofar is a Jewish instrument made from a ram's horn. How do you play it?
65179.e: You blow into the shofar like a trumpet. It has no keys and no holes.
65179.m: The shofar is a wind instrument made of horn.

65180.q: When is the baptism candle often lit again?
a: On the anniversary of the baptism
65180.e: At baptism the child is given their own candle. It is often lit again on every anniversary of the baptism.
65180.m: The baptism candle often burns again on the anniversary of the baptism.

65181.q: What colour is the sanctuary lamp in Catholic churches usually?
65181.e: The sanctuary lamp burns day and night in a lamp that is usually red. It shows that the consecrated bread is kept in the tabernacle.
65181.m: The sanctuary lamp in church usually shines red.

65182.q: What do children carry in the procession on St Martin's Day?
65182.e: On 11 November people remember Saint Martin, who shared his cloak with a beggar. Children walk through the streets with lanterns.
65182.m: On St Martin's Day children walk around with lanterns.

65183.q: What do many people put on a grave to remember someone who has died?
65183.e: A burning candle on the grave shows that you are thinking of the person. The light is a sign of hope.
65183.m: A candle on the grave remembers the dead.

65184.q: Who says in the Bible “I am the light of the world”?
65184.e: Jesus says this in the Gospel of John. That is why for Christians light is a sign of Jesus.
65184.m: Jesus calls himself the light of the world.

65185.q: At which festival in February are candles blessed in Catholic churches?
65185.e: Candlemas is on 2 February. On this day the candles for the whole year are blessed.

65186.q: What is the protective hand known in Judaism and Islam called?
65186.e: The hamsa is a hand with five fingers. It is meant to keep bad luck away and often hangs on walls or necklaces.
65186.m: The hamsa is a protective hand.

65187.q: What is often shown in the middle of the hamsa hand?
65187.e: An eye is often painted in the hand. It is meant to ward off the evil eye.
65187.m: An eye can often be seen in the hamsa hand.

65188.q: What colour is the well-known eye amulet from Turkey?
65188.e: The nazar amulet is a blue glass eye. Many people hang it in their house or car for protection.
65188.m: The Turkish protective eye is blue.

65189.q: According to Christian belief, who looks after every person?
65189.e: Many Christians believe that every person has a guardian angel. It is meant to go with them and protect them.
65189.m: A guardian angel is meant to protect every person.

65190.q: Which saint is seen as the protector of travellers?
65190.e: According to the legend, Christopher carried the baby Jesus across a river. That is why he is meant to protect everyone who is travelling.

65191.q: Which danger is Saint Florian meant to protect people from?
65191.e: Saint Florian is the patron saint of firefighters. He is often shown with a bucket of water, putting out a burning house.

65192.q: At a Hindu festival, what does a sister tie around her brother's wrist?
65192.e: At the festival of Raksha Bandhan sisters give their brothers a colourful band. It stands for protection and sticking together.
65192.m: At Raksha Bandhan the brother gets a protective band.

65193.q: What does the name Michael mean?
65193.e: Michael is a Hebrew name. It is also the name of an archangel.
65193.m: The name Michael means “Who is like God?”.

65194.q: What does the title Christ mean?
65194.e: Christ comes from a Greek word. In the past kings were anointed with oil.

65195.q: What is Mary, the mother of Jesus, called in the Quran?
65195.e: Mary is greatly honoured in the Quran. A whole sura bears her name.
65195.m: In the Quran Mary is called Maryam.

65196.q: Which name from the Bible is Ibrahim in Islam?
65196.e: Abraham is an important forefather for Jews, Christians and Muslims. That is why these three are also called Abrahamic religions.
65196.m: In Islam Abraham is called Ibrahim.

65197.q: What is the day of the saint who has the same name as you called?
65197.e: Many Catholic people celebrate their name day. Every day in the calendar belongs to one or more saints.
65197.m: On your name day you celebrate the saint with the same name.

65198.q: What do you reply to the greeting “Salam aleikum”?
65198.e: You reply to the greeting of peace with “Wa aleikum salam”. It means “And peace be with you too”.
65198.m: To “Salam aleikum” you reply “Wa aleikum salam”.

65199.q: Which country does the greeting Namaste come from?
65199.e: Namaste is a greeting from India and Nepal. It means roughly “I bow to you”.
65199.m: Namaste is a greeting from India.

65200.q: What do people do at the sign of peace in a Catholic Mass?
65200.e: At the sign of peace the people in the pews wish each other peace. As they do so, they shake hands.
65200.m: At the sign of peace people shake hands.

65201.q: In the story of Noah, what does the dove bring back to the ark?
65201.e: With the branch in its beak the dove shows that the flood is over. Trees are growing on the earth again.
65201.m: The dove brings Noah an olive branch.

65202.q: Which greeting do many Sikhs use?
65202.e: Sat Sri Akal means roughly “God is the truth”. Many Sikhs greet each other with it. Shalom is a Jewish greeting, Salam aleikum a Muslim one.
65202.m: Many Sikhs greet each other with “Sat Sri Akal”.

65203.q: What does the Latin word pax mean?
65203.e: Pax is Latin, the old language of the Church. The word can often be seen on churches or on peace flags.
65203.m: The Latin word pax means peace.

65204.q: What should you do before taking photos of people praying?
65204.e: For many people praying is something personal. That is why you first ask whether a photo is allowed.
65204.m: Before taking a photo you ask for permission.

65205.q: What should you cover with clothing when visiting many churches and temples?
65205.e: In many churches, mosques and temples people do not wear sleeveless clothes. Covered shoulders are a sign of respect.
65205.m: In many places of worship you cover your shoulders.

65206.q: What is special about the House of Religions in Bern?
a: Many religions pray under one roof
65206.e: In the House of Religions, Christians, Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists and others have their rooms. They get to know each other there.
65206.m: In the House of Religions many religions pray under one roof.

65207.q: In which city is the first mosque in Switzerland, built in 1963?
65207.e: The Mahmud Mosque stands on Forchstrasse. It has a minaret about 18 metres high.
65207.m: The first mosque in Switzerland is in Zurich.

65208.q: What is the Fraumünster in Zurich especially famous for?
65208.e: Five large, colourful stained-glass windows glow in the Fraumünster. The painter Marc Chagall made them, and they show stories from the Bible.
65208.m: The Fraumünster is famous for its colourful stained-glass windows.

65209.q: In Lausanne, who calls out the hours at night from the tower of the cathedral?
65209.e: In French the night watchman is called “le guet”. Every hour he calls “C'est le guet, il a sonné l'heure”.
65209.m: In Lausanne a night watchman calls out the hours.

65210.q: In which two villages in Aargau were Jews once the only places in Switzerland where they were allowed to live?
65210.e: Until 1866 Jews in Switzerland were only allowed to live in these two villages in the Surb valley. Old synagogues still stand there today.
65210.m: In the past Swiss Jews lived in Endingen and Lengnau.

65211.q: Who do Catholic Christians celebrate on 15 August?
65211.e: 15 August is the Assumption of Mary. In many Catholic cantons this day is a public holiday.
65211.m: On 15 August Catholics celebrate the Assumption of Mary.

65212.q: What is the holiday on 26 December called in Switzerland?
65212.e: 26 December remembers Stephen, one of the first Christians. In many cantons the day is a holiday. In Britain it is also called Boxing Day.

65213.q: What is the best-known prayer of Christians, which Jesus taught, called?
65213.e: According to the Bible, Jesus taught his disciples this prayer. It begins with the words “Our Father, who art in heaven”.
65213.m: The Lord's Prayer is the best-known prayer of Christians.

65214.q: In Islamic prayer, what touches the rug when bowing down to the ground?
65214.e: In prostration Muslims kneel and place their forehead on the floor. In this way they show humility before God.
65214.m: When praying, Muslims touch the floor with their forehead.

65215.q: What do many Catholics eat on Fridays instead of meat?
65215.e: On Friday Catholics think of the death of Jesus. That is why many go without meat on this day and eat fish.
65215.m: Many Catholics eat fish on Fridays.

65216.q: Which fish are allowed according to Jewish rules?
65216.e: Only water animals that have fins and scales are allowed. Mussels and crabs are not kosher.
65216.m: Only fish with fins and scales are kosher.

65217.q: Roughly how long does the fasting month of Ramadan last?
65217.e: Ramadan is a month in the Islamic calendar. It lasts 29 or 30 days.

65218.q: When do Muslims eat their breakfast during Ramadan?
65218.e: The meal before dawn is called suhur. After that people eat and drink nothing until the evening.
65218.m: During Ramadan people have breakfast before sunrise.

65219.q: What does a kippah look like?
65219.e: The kippah is a small round cap. It only covers a small part of the head.
65219.m: The kippah is small and round.

65220.q: What is a kippah often fastened to the hair with?
65220.e: The kippah is small and round and could easily fall off. That is why it is often fixed with a hair clip.
65220.m: A hair clip holds the kippah in place.

65221.q: What is the turban of the Sikhs called?
65221.e: Dastar is the Sikh word for their turban. It is tied afresh every day.
65221.m: The turban of the Sikhs is called a dastar.

65222.q: Roughly how long is the cloth for a Sikh turban?
65222.e: A turban needs a long strip of cloth, usually about five to six metres. It is wound around the head several times.
65222.m: A turban cloth is several metres long.

65223.q: What colour is a cardinal's head covering?
65223.e: Cardinals wear red clothes and a red skullcap. Red is a reminder of faithfulness even to the point of shedding blood.

65224.q: What did Catholic women in the past often wear on their heads in church?
65224.e: Until about 60 years ago many women covered their hair in church. Today only a few do this.
65224.m: In the past women often wore a headscarf in church.

65225.q: In which country is the place of pilgrimage Lourdes?
65225.e: Lourdes lies in the south of France at the edge of the Pyrenees. Many sick people make a pilgrimage to its spring.

65226.q: In which country does the Way of St James end?
65226.e: The Way of St James leads to Santiago de Compostela in north-west Spain. The apostle James is said to be buried there.
65226.m: The Way of St James ends in Spain.

65227.q: In which city is St Peter's Basilica?
65227.e: St Peter's Basilica stands in Vatican City in the middle of Rome. It is one of the largest churches in the world.
65227.m: St Peter's Basilica is in Rome.

65228.q: In which city is the tomb of the Prophet Muhammad?
65228.e: Muhammad is buried in Medina in Saudi Arabia. After Mecca, Medina is the second holiest city in Islam.

65229.q: In which church does the largest bell in Switzerland hang?
65229.e: The Great Bell was cast in 1611 and weighs almost 10 tonnes. It is the largest bell in Switzerland.
65229.m: The largest bell in Switzerland hangs in Bern Minster.

65230.q: What does “Allahu akbar”, the start of the call to prayer, mean?
65230.e: Allah is the Arabic word for God. “Allahu akbar” means “God is greater” or “God is great”.

65231.q: What do many muezzins use today so that the call can be heard far away?
65231.e: In the past the muezzin called using only his voice. Today loudspeakers hang on many minarets.
65231.m: Many muezzins call with loudspeakers today.

65232.q: What do many church bells ring in at midnight on New Year's Eve?
65232.e: At midnight on New Year's Eve all the bells ring in many places. In this way people welcome the new year.
65232.m: On New Year's Eve the bells ring in the new year.

65233.q: What burns in front of many Catholic churches during the Easter Vigil?
65233.e: During the Easter Vigil a fire is lit and blessed in front of the church. The large candle is lit from it.
65233.m: An Easter fire burns during the Easter Vigil.

65234.q: What do children in Switzerland carve lanterns from in November?
65234.e: Räben are white turnips. They are hollowed out, patterns are carved into them and a candle is placed inside.
65234.m: Räbeliechtli are lanterns made from turnips.

65235.q: Which saint is seen as the protector of miners and tunnel builders?
65235.e: During the building of the Gotthard Base Tunnel, too, a figure of Saint Barbara stood at the entrance. The workers asked her for protection.

65236.q: Which name is a short form of the German name Johannes?
65236.e: Johannes is an old name from the Bible; in English it is John. Hans, Jan and Jean also come from it.
65236.m: Hans is a short form of Johannes.

65237.q: In which country do people often say “Grüss Gott” as a greeting?
65237.e: “Grüss Gott” is an old greeting with a blessing. You hear it mainly in Austria and southern Germany.
65237.m: In Austria people often say “Grüss Gott”.

65238.q: Where do people never put a Quran, out of respect?
65238.e: For Muslims the Quran is the holy word of God. That is why they treat the book very carefully and do not put it on the floor.
65238.m: You do not put a Quran on the floor.

65239.q: What should you not do at a statue of the Buddha?
65239.e: For Buddhists a statue of the Buddha is something holy. Anyone who climbs or sits on it hurts the believers.
65239.m: You do not climb on a statue of the Buddha.

65240.q: Which part of another person's body do people in Thailand not touch, out of respect?
65240.e: In Thailand the head is seen as the most valuable part of the body. That is why people do not even stroke children's heads.
65240.m: In Thailand you do not touch anyone's head.

65241.q: In Switzerland, can schoolchildren get time off on the major holidays of their religion?
65241.e: In most cantons parents can make a request for major religious holidays. Then the child may stay at home.
65241.m: Children often get time off on major religious holidays.

65242.q: What do a church, a mosque and a synagogue have in common?
65242.e: All three are places of worship. People come together there to pray and to celebrate.
65242.m: Churches, mosques and synagogues are places of prayer.

65243.q: What is in a calendar of religions?
65243.e: Such a calendar shows the festivals of different religions. That way you know when your friends are celebrating something.
65243.m: A calendar of religions shows the festivals of many religions.

65244.q: What colour is the stone of Basel Minster?
65244.e: Basel Minster is built of red sandstone. It stands high above the Rhine.
65244.m: Basel Minster is made of red sandstone.

65245.q: Which reformer preached in St Pierre Cathedral in Geneva?
65245.e: John Calvin lived in Geneva in the 16th century. He made the city a centre of the Reformation.

65246.q: Which book does the Old Testament begin with?
a: With Genesis (the First Book of Moses)
65246.e: The First Book of Moses is also called Genesis, which means origin. It tells of the creation of the world.
65246.m: The Old Testament begins with Genesis.

65247.q: What does Judaism call its holy scripture, which largely matches the Old Testament?
65247.e: The name Tanakh is made from the first letters of its three parts: Teaching, Prophets and Writings. The Talmud, on the other hand, is a later collection of interpretations.
65247.m: The Jewish Bible is called the Tanakh.

65248.q: What does the word “Testament” mean in the names of the two parts of the Bible?
65248.e: The Latin word testamentum translates the Hebrew and Greek word for covenant. It means the covenant between God and people.
65248.m: In the Bible, testament means covenant.

65249.q: Which story comes right at the beginning of the Old Testament?
a: The fight between David and Goliath
65249.e: The first chapter of the Bible tells how God creates the world in six days and rests on the seventh day.
65249.m: The Bible begins with the creation of the world.

65250.q: Which Bible has more books in the Old Testament?
65250.e: Catholic Bibles contain additional later writings in the Old Testament, such as Tobit and Judith. Protestant Bibles often do not print them, or only in an appendix.
65250.m: Catholic Bibles have more books in the Old Testament.

65251.q: How many books does the New Testament have?
65251.e: The New Testament consists of the Gospels, the Acts of the Apostles, many letters and Revelation. Together there are 27 books.

65252.q: Which book does the New Testament begin with?
65252.e: The four Gospels come at the beginning of the New Testament. The first of them is the Gospel according to Matthew.
65252.m: The New Testament begins with the Gospel of Matthew.

65253.q: Roughly when were the writings of the New Testament written?
a: In the 1st and early 2nd century AD
65253.e: The texts were written down in the decades after Jesus's death. The latest writings probably date from the early 2nd century.
65253.m: The New Testament was written mostly in the 1st century AD.

65254.q: Which kind of writing makes up most of the books in the New Testament?
65254.e: More than three quarters of the books of the New Testament are letters to churches or to individual people. They explain the faith and give advice for church life.
65254.m: Most books of the New Testament are letters.

65255.q: What is at the centre of the New Testament?
a: The life, death and resurrection of Jesus
The history of the kings of Israel
65255.e: The New Testament tells of Jesus Christ and of the first Christian communities. The other topics belong to the Old Testament.
65255.m: The New Testament tells mainly of Jesus Christ.

65256.q: What are the names of the four Evangelists?
65256.e: The four Gospels in the New Testament are named after them. Each tells of the life and work of Jesus in its own way.
65256.m: The four Evangelists are Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

65257.q: Which three Gospels tell many of the same stories about Jesus?
65257.e: Matthew, Mark and Luke are very similar; they are called the synoptic Gospels. The Gospel of John tells many things quite differently.
65257.m: Matthew, Mark and Luke tell many of the same stories.

65259.q: Which Gospel begins with the words “In the beginning was the Word”?
65259.e: John does not begin with the birth of Jesus, but with a solemn text about the divine Word. This opening deliberately recalls the beginning of the Bible.
65259.m: The Gospel of John begins with “In the beginning was the Word”.

65260.q: Which of the four Gospels is the shortest?
65260.e: The Gospel of Mark has only 16 chapters. It tells its story briefly and begins straight away with the appearance of John the Baptist.
65260.m: The Gospel of Mark is the shortest Gospel.

65261.q: Which Gospel is the only one to tell of the raising of Lazarus?
65261.e: In chapter 11, Jesus calls his dead friend Lazarus out of the tomb. The other Gospels do not report this.
65261.m: The raising of Lazarus is only in the Gospel of John.

65262.q: Which animal is the symbol of the Evangelist Mark?
65262.e: Each Evangelist has a symbol, and Mark's is the lion. That is why the lion of St Mark is also the emblem of Venice, where his relics are venerated.
65262.m: The lion is the sign of the Evangelist Mark.

65263.q: Which animal is the symbol of the Evangelist John?
65263.e: The eagle stands for the lofty, spiritual view of John's Gospel. That is why many church pictures show John with an eagle.
65263.m: John has the eagle as his symbol.

65264.q: In which Gospel is the Sermon on the Mount?
65264.e: The Sermon on the Mount is in chapters 5 to 7 of Matthew. It contains, for example, the Beatitudes and the Lord's Prayer.
65264.m: The Sermon on the Mount is found in the Gospel of Matthew.

65265.q: How many letters in the New Testament name Paul as the sender?
65265.e: Thirteen letters begin with Paul's name. However, scholars consider only seven of them to be certainly written by him.
65265.m: Thirteen letters in the New Testament bear Paul's name.

65266.q: Which of Paul's letters comes first in the New Testament?
65266.e: Paul's letters are arranged roughly by length. The letter to the church in Rome is the longest and therefore comes first.
65266.m: Romans is the first and longest of Paul's letters.

65267.q: What does Paul write in Galatians about Jews and Greeks, slaves and free people?
65267.e: In chapter 3 of Galatians, Paul stresses that all who are baptised are of equal worth, no matter where they come from.
65267.m: In Galatians, Paul writes that all are one in Christ.

65268.q: According to Paul's “hymn to love”, what is the greatest?
65268.e: In First Corinthians, Paul writes: faith, hope and love remain, but the greatest of these is love.
65268.m: For Paul, love is the greatest.

65269.q: What does Paul ask for in his short letter to Philemon?
a: To welcome a runaway slave like a brother
To collect money for a journey to Rome
To go on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem
65269.e: Paul asks Philemon to take back his slave Onesimus, and to do so as a brother. It is the shortest of Paul's letters.
65269.m: In the letter to Philemon, Paul speaks up for a slave.

65270.q: Who are most of Paul's letters addressed to?
65270.e: Paul founded and visited churches, for example in Corinth, Philippi and Thessalonica. With letters he advised them from afar.
65270.m: Paul wrote most of his letters to Christian communities.

65271.q: What does the Latin word “pastor” mean, after which the letters to Timothy and Titus are called the Pastoral Letters?
65271.e: The letters give advice on how to lead a church like a good shepherd. That is why they are called the Pastoral Letters.

65272.q: Why are Philippians and some other letters of Paul called “prison letters”?
a: Paul wrote them as a prisoner
They were found in a prison
65272.e: In these letters, Paul mentions that he is in custody. Even so, he encourages the churches in them.
65272.m: Paul wrote the prison letters while he was in custody.

65273.q: How many psalms does the Book of Psalms contain?
65273.e: The Book of Psalms is a collection of 150 songs and prayers. It is one of the longest books of the Bible.

65274.q: With which words does Psalm 23 begin?
a: “Hear, O Israel, the Lord is one”
65274.e: Psalm 23 compares God to a shepherd who takes care of his sheep. It is one of the best-known texts in the Bible.
65274.m: Psalm 23 begins with “The Lord is my shepherd”.

65275.q: What are the psalms in the Bible?
65275.e: The psalms are songs and prayers. Many praise God, others lament or ask for help.

65276.q: How long are the psalms in the Bible?
a: Very different, from two to over 170 verses
Every psalm is exactly one page long
65276.e: Psalm 117 has only two verses, while Psalm 119 has 176 verses. That also makes it the longest chapter in the Bible.

65277.q: What does the shortest psalm, Psalm 117, call on all nations to do?
65277.e: Psalm 117 has only two verses. It calls on all nations to praise God.
65277.m: The shortest psalm calls people to praise God.

65278.q: What does the Hebrew word “Hallelujah”, which often appears in the psalms, mean?
65278.e: Hallelujah literally means “Praise Yah”, a short form of the name of God. It is a call to praise God.

65279.q: Which Swiss anthem has a name that recalls the biblical Book of Psalms?
65279.e: The Swiss Psalm was set to music in 1841 by the monk Alberich Zwyssig. Since 1981 it has been the official national anthem of Switzerland.
65279.m: The Swiss national anthem is called the Swiss Psalm.

65280.q: Which king is credited with a large number of the psalms?
65280.e: Many psalms carry the heading “of David”. David is said to have played the harp and written songs for God.
65280.m: Many psalms are credited to King David.

65281.q: Which event is told at the beginning of the Acts of the Apostles?
a: The birth of Jesus in Bethlehem
The baptism of Jesus in the Jordan
65281.e: In the first chapter, Jesus is taken up into heaven before the eyes of the disciples. After that, the story of the first church begins.
65281.m: The Acts of the Apostles begins with the ascension of Jesus.

65282.q: According to Acts, who gradually became allowed to belong to the Christian community too?
a: People who were not Jews as well
65282.e: Peter baptised the Roman centurion Cornelius and his family. With this, the community opened up to non-Jews as well.
65282.m: The community opened up to non-Jews as well.

65283.q: What does the story of Ananias and Sapphira in Acts warn against?
65283.e: The two secretly kept part of the money from a field and claimed they had given everything. The story warns against dishonesty.
65283.m: Ananias and Sapphira lied and were punished.

65284.q: According to Acts, who was freed from prison by an angel at night, even though he was chained to guards?
65284.e: King Herod Agrippa had Peter locked up. An angel loosened the chains and led him out.
65284.m: An angel freed Peter from prison.

65285.q: According to Acts, on which island was Paul shipwrecked on the way to Rome?
65285.e: The ship was wrecked in a storm, but everyone reached the shore. The bay on Malta is still named after Paul today.

65286.q: How does the Acts of the Apostles end?
a: Paul lives in Rome under guard and keeps preaching
65286.e: In the last chapter, Paul lives for two years in a rented house in Rome and is guarded. The book does not report his death.
65286.m: The Acts of the Apostles ends with Paul in Rome.

65287.q: According to Acts, what did the first church in Jerusalem choose special helpers for?
a: To care for the poor and widows
65287.e: The apostles wanted to concentrate on prayer and preaching. So seven men were appointed to care for the poor; this is seen as the beginning of the office of deacon.
65287.m: The early church chose helpers for the poor.

65288.q: Roughly in which years was the Gutenberg Bible printed?
65288.e: The printing took about two to three years. As early as 1455, the later Pope Enea Silvio Piccolomini wrote in a letter about finished sheets he had seen.
65288.m: The Gutenberg Bible was printed from about 1452 to 1454.

65289.q: Which book comes right at the end of the Christian Bible?
65289.e: Revelation describes in visions the end of the old world and a new creation. That is why it fits at the end of the Bible.
65289.m: The Bible ends with the Revelation to John.

65290.q: On which island is John said to have received his visions of Revelation?
65290.e: John himself writes that he was on the island of Patmos in the Aegean. A grotto there that recalls him is still shown today.
65290.m: John had his visions on the island of Patmos.

65291.q: What does the Greek word “apocalypse”, the other name for Revelation, literally mean?
65291.e: Apocalypse literally means “uncovering” or “unveiling”. Only later did the word become an everyday term for disasters.

65292.q: To how many churches in Asia Minor are the letters at the beginning of Revelation addressed?
65292.e: The letters go to churches including those in Ephesus, Smyrna and Pergamon. In the Bible, the number seven often stands for completeness.
65292.m: Revelation contains seven letters to churches.

65293.q: Which number is called the “number of the beast” in Revelation?
65293.e: In chapter 13, the number 666 stands for a hostile beast. Some old manuscripts have the number 616 instead.
65293.m: The number of the beast in Revelation is 666.

65294.q: In Revelation, who opens the scroll with the seven seals?
a: A lamb as an image of Christ
65294.e: Only the Lamb is worthy to open the seals. The Lamb stands for Jesus Christ, who was sacrificed and lives.
65294.m: In Revelation, the Lamb opens the seven seals.

65295.q: What does John see at the end of Revelation?
a: A new heaven and a new earth
The building of the Tower of Babel
65295.e: At the end, John describes the heavenly Jerusalem, where there is no more suffering. The other images come from the Old Testament.
65295.m: Revelation ends with the vision of a new world.

65296.q: In Revelation, what is the place called where the kings gather for the final battle?
65296.e: The name Armageddon is often linked to the hill of Megiddo in Israel. Today the word is used in everyday language for a huge disaster.
65296.m: In Revelation, Armageddon is the place of the final battle.

65297.q: What is the Greek name of the First Book of Moses?
65297.e: Genesis means origin or beginning. The book tells of the beginnings of the world and of people.
65297.m: The First Book of Moses is called Genesis.

65298.q: What is told right at the beginning of the First Book of Moses?
65298.e: The Bible begins with the creation of the world in six days and the day of rest. Only after that come other stories such as the Flood.
65298.m: The Bible begins with the creation story.

65299.q: What does the Second Book of Moses, Exodus, mainly tell about?
a: The building of the Temple in Jerusalem
65299.e: Exodus means going out. Moses leads the people of Israel out of slavery in Egypt into freedom.
65299.m: The Second Book of Moses tells of the exodus from Egypt.

65300.q: Which of the five Books of Moses contains many rules for priests and sacrifices?
65300.e: The name recalls the tribe of Levi, from which the priests came. The book contains rules for worship, sacrifices and purity.
65300.m: Leviticus is the book of rules for priests.

65301.q: What does Judaism call the five Books of Moses?
65301.e: Torah means instruction or teaching. In the synagogue it is read aloud from a handwritten scroll.
65301.m: In Judaism, the five Books of Moses are called the Torah.

65302.q: Which of the five Books of Moses has a Greek name meaning “second law”?
65302.e: In Deuteronomy, Moses repeats the commandments once more for the people before he dies. That is where the name “second law” comes from.
65302.m: The fifth Book of Moses is called Deuteronomy.

65303.q: Why is the fourth Book of Moses called “Numbers”?
a: Because the people of Israel are counted in it
Because it contains rules for arithmetic
Because it is the shortest book
Because it counts the years of the kings
65303.e: At the beginning and again later, this book describes a census. After that it tells of the long journey through the desert.
65303.m: The Book of Numbers is named after the censuses.

65304.q: Who led the people of Israel into the promised land after Moses died?
65304.e: Moses was only allowed to see the promised land from a mountain. After his death, Joshua led the people across the Jordan.
65304.m: Joshua led Israel into the promised land.

65305.q: Which forefather of the people of Israel is called by God to a new land in the First Book of Moses?
65305.e: God tells Abraham to leave his homeland and promises him many descendants. Abraham is seen as the forefather of Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
65305.m: Abraham is the great forefather in the First Book of Moses.

65306.q: Of which biblical book was an almost complete scroll over 2000 years old found at Qumran by the Dead Sea?
65306.e: The Great Isaiah Scroll was discovered in a cave in 1947. It is one of the oldest surviving manuscripts of the Bible.
65306.m: The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran is over 2000 years old.

65307.q: In which city did the prophet Isaiah work?
65307.e: Isaiah lived in Jerusalem and advised the kings of Judah there. His messages were directed mainly at this city.
65307.m: The prophet Isaiah worked in Jerusalem.

65308.q: Which image of peace from the Book of Isaiah became the motto of many peace movements?
a: “An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth”
65308.e: Isaiah 2 says that the nations will beat their swords into ploughshares. So weapons are turned into tools for farming.
65308.m: “Swords into ploughshares” is an image of peace from the Book of Isaiah.

65309.q: When did the prophet Isaiah live?
a: At the same time as Jesus
65309.e: Isaiah worked in Jerusalem from about 740 BC, so about 700 years before the birth of Jesus.
65309.m: Isaiah lived about 700 years before Jesus.

65310.q: Which empire conquered Jerusalem and destroyed the Temple in the time of the prophet Jeremiah?
65310.e: King Nebuchadnezzar II conquered Jerusalem in 587 or 586 BC. Many people were taken into exile in Babylon.
65310.m: In Jeremiah's time, the Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem.

65311.q: What was the task of a prophet like Jeremiah?
a: To proclaim God's message to the people
To rule the people as king
65311.e: Prophets spoke on God's behalf. Jeremiah warned his people and announced disaster if they did not change.

65312.q: Which word for a long speech of complaint comes from the name of the prophet Jeremiah?
65312.e: Jeremiah had to announce a lot of disaster and often lamented about his people. That is why a long moan is called a jeremiad today.
65312.m: A jeremiad is a long speech of complaint.

65313.q: In which part of the Bible is the Book of Jeremiah?
a: In the Acts of the Apostles
65313.e: Jeremiah is one of the major prophets of the Old Testament. He lived several hundred years before Jesus.
65313.m: Jeremiah is a prophet of the Old Testament.

65314.q: In which language is most of the Old Testament written?
65314.e: The Old Testament is the Bible of the people of Israel and was therefore written in their language. Only a few chapters are written in another language.
65314.m: The Old Testament is mostly written in Hebrew.

65315.q: In which language were the writings of the New Testament written?
65315.e: At that time, Greek was the common language of the eastern Mediterranean. So the texts could be read in many countries.
65315.m: The New Testament was written in Greek.

65316.q: In which direction is Hebrew written?
65316.e: That is why Hebrew books are opened from what is, for us, the back. Arabic is also written from right to left.
65316.m: Hebrew is written from right to left.

65317.q: Into which language was the Old Testament translated even before Christ, so that Jews in Egypt could read it too?
65317.e: The translation was made from the 3rd century BC in Alexandria and is called the Septuagint, which means “seventy”.
65317.m: The Old Testament was translated into Greek early on.

65318.q: Into which language did Jerome translate the Bible around AD 400?
65318.e: Jerome's Latin Bible is called the Vulgate. In the West it was the most important Bible for over 1000 years.
65318.m: Jerome translated the Bible into Latin.

65319.q: What was missing in the original Hebrew writing of the Bible?
65319.e: The Bible was first written down with consonants only. Only in the Middle Ages did Jewish scholars, the Masoretes, add dots and dashes for the vowels.
65319.m: The Hebrew Bible was originally written without vowels.

65320.q: Where does the word “Bible” come from?
a: From the Greek word for books
From the Latin word for law
From the Hebrew word for God
From the German word for praying
65320.e: The Greek biblia means “books”. The Bible really is a collection of many separate books.

65321.q: From which languages did Luther translate the Bible into German?
65321.e: The Old Testament is written in Hebrew, the New Testament in Greek. Luther translated from these original languages.
65321.m: Luther translated from Hebrew and Greek.

65322.q: In which castle did Luther translate the New Testament while he was in hiding?
65322.e: After the Diet of Worms, Luther hid at Wartburg Castle. There he translated the New Testament in just a few weeks.
65322.m: Luther translated the New Testament at Wartburg Castle.

65323.q: In Luther's time, what did the German word “dolmetschen” mean?
65323.e: In 1530 Luther wrote the “Sendbrief vom Dolmetschen” (Open Letter on Translating). In it he explained how he had translated the Bible.

65324.q: Which Bible translation is still the most widely used in the Protestant churches of Germany today?
65324.e: The Luther Bible is used as the main text in services of the Protestant churches in Germany. The Unity Translation, on the other hand, is mainly Catholic.
65324.m: The Luther Bible is the most important Protestant Bible in Germany.

65325.q: In which town was the first complete Luther Bible printed?
65325.e: Luther taught at the university of this town, where the Bible was also printed. The town thus became a centre of the Reformation.
65325.m: The first complete Luther Bible was printed in Wittenberg.

65326.q: For which occasion did the latest revision of the Luther Bible appear in 2017?
a: For the 500th anniversary of the Reformation
For the founding of the European Union
For the 100th anniversary of the Bible Society
65326.e: In 1517 Luther published his theses, which is seen as the start of the Reformation. For the anniversary in 2017, a newly revised Luther Bible appeared.
65326.m: The Luther Bible 2017 appeared for the Reformation anniversary.

65327.q: What did Luther mainly want to achieve with his Bible translation?
a: That ordinary people understand the Bible
That only priests read the Bible
That everyone has to learn Latin
65327.e: In his own words, Luther wanted to “look at people's mouths” and write the way people spoke. That way many could read the Bible themselves or have it read to them.
65327.m: Luther translated the Bible so that everyone could understand it.

65328.q: What effect did the Luther Bible have on the German language?
a: It helped shape a common written language
65328.e: The Luther Bible was read in all German-speaking areas. Its words and phrases did a lot to standardise High German.
65328.m: The Luther Bible helped shape written High German.

65329.q: Which Zurich reformer started the Zurich Bible?
65329.e: Zwingli wanted the congregation to be able to read the Bible in their own language. He translated together with other Zurich theologians.
65329.m: The Zurich Bible goes back to the reformer Zwingli.

65330.q: Why is the Zurich Bible revised again and again?
a: Because the old Bibles are banned
Because the original text was lost
Because every church wants its own Bible
65330.e: Words and sentences change over the centuries. That is why the Zurich Bible was revised in 1931 and 2007, for example.
65330.m: Bibles are retranslated because language changes.

65331.q: Which part of the Zurich Bible appeared first, from 1524?
65331.e: First the text about Jesus and the apostles came out, then the Old Testament step by step. Finally all the parts were brought together in one volume.
65331.m: The New Testament of the Zurich Bible appeared first.

65332.q: In which city did Leo Jud work as a minister and help Zwingli translate the Bible?
65332.e: Leo Jud was minister at St Peter's Church in Zurich. He was one of the most important translators of the Zurich Bible.
65332.m: Leo Jud worked on the Bible translation in Zurich.

65333.q: Roughly how long did experts work on the new Zurich Bible, which appeared in 2007?
65333.e: Experts worked for about two decades on the new translation. In 2007 it was presented in the Grossmünster.
65333.m: The new Zurich Bible appeared in 2007.

65334.q: Which church publishes the Zurich Bible today?
a: The Reformed Church of the Canton of Zurich
The Roman Catholic Diocese of Chur
The Christian Catholic Church of Switzerland
65334.e: The Zurich Bible is the Bible of the Reformed tradition from Zurich. The cantonal church is responsible for its revisions.
65334.m: The Reformed Church of Zurich publishes the Zurich Bible.

65335.q: What is the Zurich Bible especially known for among German translations?
a: For staying very close to the original text
65335.e: The Zurich Bible translates very precisely from the Hebrew and Greek text. That is why it is often used for studying the Bible.
65335.m: The Zurich Bible translates especially closely to the original text.

65336.q: In which ancient languages did the Zurich scholars read the Bible before translating it?
65336.e: The Old Testament is written in Hebrew, the New Testament in Greek. In the Zurich Prophezei, scholars read these texts every day.
65336.m: The Bible was translated from Hebrew and Greek.

65337.q: In which city was the Gutenberg Bible printed?
65337.e: Johannes Gutenberg ran his printing workshop in his home town on the Rhine. Today the city is in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.
65337.m: The Gutenberg Bible was printed in Mainz.

65338.q: How many lines does a column of the Gutenberg Bible usually have?
65338.e: Each page has two columns with usually 42 lines. That is why it is also called the 42-line Bible, or B42 for short.
65338.m: The Gutenberg Bible usually has 42 lines per column.

65339.q: Roughly how many copies of the Gutenberg Bible were printed?
65339.e: For the time, that was a large print run. Copying a manuscript by hand, by contrast, often took years.

65340.q: Why are Gutenberg Bibles so valuable today?
a: Because only a few have survived
Because they are made of gold
Because Gutenberg wrote each one himself
Because they are the first book in German
65340.e: Of about 180 printed copies, 49 are still known today, complete or in part. They are among the most expensive books in the world.
65340.m: Gutenberg Bibles are very rare and valuable.

65341.q: What was new about the way Gutenberg produced his Bible?
a: He printed with movable metal letters
He copied every page by hand
He carved every page in stone
65341.e: Gutenberg cast individual letters from metal that could be put together again and again. This made it possible to print many identical pages quickly.
65341.m: Gutenberg printed with movable metal letters.

65342.q: What was the Gutenberg Bible printed on?
a: On paper and partly on parchment
65342.e: Most copies were made on paper, a smaller number on expensive parchment made from animal skin. Red headings were added later by hand.
65342.m: The Gutenberg Bible exists on paper and on parchment.

65343.q: Which festival is seen as the birthday of the Church, because the first community in Jerusalem began on this day?
65343.e: According to the Acts of the Apostles, the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples at Pentecost. After that many people were baptised, and the first community began.
65343.m: Pentecost is seen as the birthday of the Church.

65344.q: According to Acts, how many people were baptised after Peter's sermon at Pentecost?
65344.e: Acts 2:41 says that about 3000 people were added on that day.
65344.m: After the Pentecost sermon, about 3000 people were baptised.

65345.q: Which book of the Bible tells mainly about the life of the first Christians after Jesus's ascension?
65345.e: The Acts of the Apostles is the fifth book of the New Testament. It reports on the first churches and the spread of the faith.
65345.m: The Acts of the Apostles tells the story of the first Christians.

65346.q: Which Evangelist is traditionally credited with writing the Acts of the Apostles?
65346.e: The Acts of the Apostles is seen as the second part of the Gospel of Luke. Both books are addressed to a certain Theophilus.
65346.m: Luke is seen as the author of the Acts of the Apostles.

65347.q: According to Acts, how did the members of the first church live with their possessions?
a: They gave everything to the emperor
65347.e: According to Acts, the believers had “everything in common”. This is called community of goods, so that nobody had to suffer need.
65347.m: The first church shared its possessions in common.

65348.q: Who is regarded as the first Christian martyr?
65348.e: Stephen was one of the seven helpers who cared for the poor in the church. He was stoned in Jerusalem.
65348.m: Stephen was the first Christian martyr.

65349.q: According to the New Testament, which brother of Jesus became a leader of the church in Jerusalem?
65349.e: In Galatians, Paul names James, the brother of the Lord, as one of the pillars of the Jerusalem church. James also plays an important role at the Council of Jerusalem.
65349.m: James, the brother of Jesus, helped lead the church in Jerusalem.

65350.q: What were the followers of Jesus called for the first time in the city of Antioch?
65350.e: Acts 11:26 reports that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch. The name comes from Christ.
65350.m: The name “Christians” first appeared in Antioch.

65351.q: What did the apostles decide around AD 48 at the Council of Jerusalem?
a: Non-Jews do not have to keep all Jewish laws
The Bible will be translated into Latin
65351.e: The apostles agreed that Christians from other peoples did not have to keep the whole Jewish law. This made mission outside Judaism easier.
65351.m: The Council of Jerusalem opened the Church to non-Jews.

65352.q: By which name is Paul first called in the Acts of the Apostles?
65352.e: Paul had the Jewish name Saul. Paul was his Roman name.
65352.m: In Acts, Paul is first called Saul.

65353.q: In which city was Paul born?
65353.e: Paul came from Tarsus in Cilicia, in the south of present-day Turkey. That is why he is also called Paul of Tarsus.

65354.q: According to the Bible, on the way to which city was Paul converted?
65354.e: Paul wanted to persecute Christians in Damascus. On the way, according to Acts, a bright light appeared to him and he heard the voice of Jesus.

65355.q: With which trade did Paul earn his living?
65355.e: According to Acts 18:3, Paul worked as a tentmaker. That way he did not have to be paid by the churches.

65356.q: According to Acts, how many missionary journeys of Paul are usually counted?
65356.e: Three missionary journeys through Asia Minor and Greece are counted. After that, Paul came to Rome as a prisoner.

65357.q: Who went with Paul on his first missionary journey?
65357.e: Barnabas and Paul were sent out together by their church. The journey took them to Cyprus, among other places.
65357.m: Barnabas was Paul's companion on the first missionary journey.

65358.q: To which continent was Paul one of the first to bring Christianity when he travelled to Greece?
65358.e: In Philippi in Macedonia, Paul founded the first Christian church in Europe. There the purple-cloth trader Lydia was baptised.

65359.q: In which Greek city did Paul give a famous speech about the “unknown god”?
65359.e: Paul spoke in Athens on the Areopagus hill. He started from an altar “to an unknown god”.
65359.m: Paul preached in Athens about the unknown god.

65360.q: Which are older: Paul's letters or the Gospels?
a: Both were written in the same year
65360.e: Paul wrote his letters from about AD 50. The Gospels were written only a few decades later.
65360.m: Paul's letters are older than the Gospels.

65361.q: Which title was Paul given because he mainly preached to non-Jews?
65361.e: Paul saw himself as the apostle of the Gentiles, meaning the non-Jews. That is why he is also called the Apostle to the Gentiles.
65361.m: Paul is called the Apostle to the Gentiles.

65362.q: What was the apostle Peter's original name?
65362.e: Peter was actually called Simon. Jesus gave him the new name Cephas, Petros in Greek.

65363.q: What job did Peter do before he followed Jesus?
65363.e: Peter fished with his brother on the Sea of Galilee. Jesus promised to make him a “fisher of men”.
65363.m: Peter was a fisherman by trade.

65364.q: What does the name Peter mean when translated?
65364.e: Peter comes from the Greek word for stone or rock. According to the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus said he would build his church on this rock.

65365.q: According to tradition, how did Peter die in Rome?
65365.e: According to old tradition, Peter did not want to die in the same way as Jesus. So he is said to have been crucified head down.
65365.m: According to tradition, Peter was crucified upside down.

65366.q: According to tradition, under which Roman emperor did Peter die?
65366.e: Tradition places Peter's death in the time of the persecution of Christians under Nero in the 60s. An exact date is not certain.
65366.m: According to tradition, Peter died under Emperor Nero.

65367.q: Where is Peter's tomb said to be?
a: Under St Peter's Basilica in the Vatican
65367.e: Excavations under St Peter's Basilica found a tomb that has been venerated as Peter's tomb since the 2nd century. The high altar stands above it.
65367.m: Peter's tomb is venerated under St Peter's Basilica.

65369.q: Which object is Peter's best-known emblem in art?
65369.e: According to the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus promised Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven. That is why he is often shown with keys.
65369.m: In pictures, Peter can be recognised by his keys.

65370.q: According to legend, what Latin question did Peter ask Jesus while fleeing Rome?
65370.e: According to legend, Peter met Jesus while fleeing and asked: “Where are you going, Lord?” Then he returned to Rome.

65371.q: After which event in AD 64 did Emperor Nero have Christians persecuted?
a: After the Great Fire of Rome
65371.e: A large part of Rome burnt down in the year 64. Nero blamed the Christians to draw rumours away from himself.
65371.m: Nero blamed the Christians for the fire of Rome.

65372.q: What are the underground burial places of the early Christians in Rome called?
65372.e: The early Christians buried their dead in the catacombs. They lie outside the old city walls of Rome.
65372.m: The early Christians in Rome were buried in catacombs.

65373.q: Why did Christians in the Roman Empire often come into conflict with the state?
a: They refused to sacrifice to the emperor
They built palaces that were too big
65373.e: In the imperial cult, people were supposed to sacrifice to the emperor as a divine ruler. Christians refused, because they worshipped only one God.
65373.m: Christians refused to sacrifice to the emperor.

65374.q: What did Emperor Decius demand of all inhabitants of the empire around AD 250?
a: To sacrifice to the Roman gods
65374.e: Anyone who sacrificed received a certificate. Christians who refused were punished. It was the first persecution throughout the whole empire.
65374.m: Under Decius, everyone had to sacrifice to the gods.

65375.q: Which emperor allowed Christians to live their faith freely in 313?
65375.e: With the Edict of Milan in 313, the persecutions ended. Shortly before, Diocletian had ordered the greatest persecution of Christians.
65375.m: Constantine ended the persecution of Christians in 313.

65376.q: What does the Greek word “martyr” originally mean?
65376.e: A martyr bears witness to their faith even unto death. That is where the meaning “witness” comes from.

65377.q: What is the name of the leader of the Theban Legion, after whom a town in Valais is named?
65377.e: According to legend, Maurice and his Christian soldiers were executed near Agaunum because they refused to kill Christians or to sacrifice to the gods. Today the town is called Saint-Maurice VS.
65377.m: Saint-Maurice in Valais is named after the martyr Maurice.

65378.q: According to legend, which two martyrs are the patron saints of the city of Zurich?
65378.e: Felix and Regula are said to have been beheaded as Christians in Zurich. They still appear on the city's seal today.
65378.m: Felix and Regula are the patron saints of Zurich.

65379.q: Which two martyrs of the Theban Legion are honoured as the patron saints of Solothurn?
65379.e: According to legend, Ursus and Victor died as martyrs in Solothurn. Solothurn Cathedral is dedicated to them and is called St Ursus Cathedral.
65379.m: Ursus and Victor are the patron saints of Solothurn.

65380.q: What are the catacombs in Rome?
65380.e: Catacombs are long underground passages with graves. Christians buried their dead there.

65381.q: Why were the catacombs outside the city walls of Rome?
a: Burials in the city were forbidden
The ground there was made of gold
65381.e: Under Roman law, the dead could not be buried inside the city. That is why cemeteries lay along the roads leading out of town.
65381.m: Romans were not allowed to bury their dead in the city.

65382.q: Into which soft rock were the catacombs of Rome dug?
65382.e: Volcanic tuff is soft enough to dig, but hardens in the air. This allowed passages to be made over several levels.
65382.m: The catacombs were dug into soft tuff.

65383.q: How were the dead usually buried in the catacombs?
a: In glass coffins on the floor
65383.e: The graves were cut into the walls as rectangular niches one above the other and closed with slabs.
65383.m: In the catacombs, the dead lay in wall niches.

65384.q: On which famous Roman road are the Catacomb of Callixtus and the Catacomb of St Sebastian?
65384.e: The Via Appia leads south from Rome. Several important catacombs lie along it.
65384.m: Well-known catacombs lie along the Via Appia.

65385.q: Why did the early Christians prefer burial to cremation?
a: Because of their belief in the resurrection
65385.e: Christians believed in the resurrection of the dead. That is why they wanted to bury the body, as had also happened with Jesus.
65385.m: Because of their belief in the resurrection, Christians preferred burial.

65386.q: Which image of Jesus is found especially often in the paintings of the catacombs?
65386.e: The Good Shepherd carries a sheep on his shoulders. The picture shows Jesus taking care of his own.
65386.m: The Good Shepherd is a common image in the catacombs.

65387.q: How do many figures in the pictures in the catacombs pray?
65387.e: The figure with outstretched, raised arms is called an orant. This prayer posture was common in ancient times.
65387.m: Early Christians often prayed with raised arms.

65388.q: Which animal served early Christians as a secret sign of recognition, including in the catacombs?
65388.e: The Greek word for fish, “Ichthys”, contains the first letters of “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Saviour”.
65388.m: The fish is an early Christian sign.

65389.q: What does the Greek word “Ichthys” mean?
65389.e: Ichthys is the Greek word for fish. The fish became an early sign of recognition for Christians.

65390.q: In which language is the word Ichthys written?
65390.e: In the eastern Mediterranean, Greek was the common language at that time. Many early Christians spoke and wrote Greek.

65391.q: What do the first letters of the word Ichthys stand for?
a: Jesus Christ, Son of God, Saviour
65391.e: The Greek letters I, CH, TH, Y and S are the first letters of the words “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Saviour”. So the fish becomes a statement of faith.
65391.m: Ichthys stands for Jesus Christ, Son of God, Saviour.

65392.q: What is a word formed from the first letters of other words, like Ichthys, called?
65392.e: In an acrostic, the first letters of words or lines make a new word. Ichthys is a well-known example.

65393.q: According to a well-known story, how is the fish sign said to have been used as a sign of recognition?
a: One person drew a curve, the other completed the fish
People carried a real fish with them
People painted the fish on every front door
65393.e: According to this story, one person drew a curve in the sand. Anyone who was also a Christian added the second curve. Whether it really happened like this is not proven.
65393.m: Christians are said to have recognised each other by half a fish in the sand.

65394.q: Why does the fish sign go well with baptism?
a: Because water is used at baptism
Because people eat fish after baptism
Because baptism must always be by the sea
Because fishermen were the first priests
65394.e: Fish live in water, and water is used at baptism. As early as around 200, Tertullian compared baptised Christians to little fish.
65394.m: Water links the fish and baptism.

65395.q: Which image was often used in the catacombs as a sign of hope, because it holds a ship steady?
65395.e: The anchor holds a ship steady in a storm. For the early Christians it was an image of hope, and its shape recalled a cross.
65395.m: The anchor was an early Christian sign of hope.

65396.q: Why did the cross only later become the most common Christian symbol?
a: Crucifixion was seen as a shameful execution
The cross was a sign of the emperors
The cross was not yet known
65396.e: In the Roman Empire, crucifixion was a particularly humiliating death penalty. Only after Constantine had abolished it did the cross gradually become a widespread sign.
65396.m: The cross only became established as a sign after crucifixions ended.

65397.q: Which letters mean “beginning and end” and often appear next to early Christian signs for Christ?
65397.e: Alpha is the first and Omega the last letter of the Greek alphabet. In Revelation, Christ says: “I am the Alpha and the Omega.”
65397.m: Alpha and Omega stand for beginning and end.

65398.q: Which religion did Emperor Constantine help to break through in the Roman Empire?
65398.e: Constantine supported the Christians, had churches built and was baptised before his death.

65399.e: Constantine was a Roman emperor. From 324 he ruled the whole empire alone.

65400.q: According to the Christian writer Lactantius, which sign did Constantine have painted on his soldiers' shields before the Battle of the Milvian Bridge?
65400.e: Lactantius reports that Constantine was told in a dream to put a sign of Christ on the shields. The Chi-Rho monogram is made of the Greek letters Chi and Rho.
65400.m: Constantine fought under the Chi-Rho monogram.

65401.q: Which city did Constantine make the new capital of the empire in 330?
65401.e: Constantine enlarged the city of Byzantium and named it after himself. Today it is called Istanbul.
65401.m: Constantinople, today's Istanbul, was Constantine's city.

65402.q: Which day of the week did Constantine set as a day of rest in 321?
65402.e: Constantine decreed that courts and craftsmen should rest on the “venerable day of the sun”. For Christians it was the day of the resurrection.
65402.m: Since Constantine, Sunday has been a day of rest.

65403.q: What was the name of Constantine's mother, who travelled to the Holy Land?
65403.e: Helena travelled to Palestine around 326 and supported the building of churches there. Legend says she found the cross of Jesus.

65404.q: As what is Constantine honoured in the Orthodox Church?
65404.e: In the Orthodox Church, Constantine is regarded as a saint because of his importance for Christianity.
65404.m: The Orthodox honour Constantine as a saint.

65405.q: Which church did Constantine have built in Jerusalem over the place where Jesus is said to have been buried?
a: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre
65405.e: Constantine had a Roman temple there pulled down and a large church built. It was consecrated in 335 and is still an important place of pilgrimage today.
65405.m: Constantine had the Church of the Holy Sepulchre built in Jerusalem.

65406.q: What did the Milan agreement allow Christians to do?
65406.e: In 313 the emperors agreed in Milan that everyone, including Christians, could practise their religion freely.
65406.m: From 313, Christians could live their faith freely.

65407.q: Which two emperors made the Milan agreement?
65407.e: The two rulers shared the empire at that time. In Milan they agreed on a common religious policy.
65407.m: Constantine and Licinius made the Milan agreement.

65408.q: According to the Milan agreement, what were Christians to get back?
65408.e: During the persecution, the state had seized the Christians' buildings and land. These were now to be returned.
65408.m: Christians got back their confiscated meeting places.

65409.q: By which other name is the Milan agreement often known?
65409.e: In the past people usually spoke of the Edict of Milan. Because no actual edict was issued, today it is often called an agreement.
65409.m: The Milan agreement is also called the Edict of Milan.

65410.q: Which emperor allowed Christians their faith in 313 with the Milan agreement?
65410.e: In 313 in Milan, Emperor Constantine agreed with his co-emperor Licinius that all people could freely choose their religion. This ended the persecution of Christians.
65410.m: Constantine allowed Christians their faith in 313.

65411.q: Did the Milan agreement make Christianity the state religion?
a: No, it only allowed all religions
Yes, immediately for the whole empire
65411.e: The agreement put Christianity on an equal footing with the other religions. It only became the state religion several decades later.
65411.m: The Milan agreement did not make Christianity the state religion.

65412.q: What was the city of Milan called in Roman times?
65412.e: In the 4th century, Mediolanum was at times the emperor's residence in the West. That is why the emperors met there.
65412.m: In Roman times, Milan was called Mediolanum.

65413.q: Which group was often persecuted in the Roman Empire before the Milan agreement?
65413.e: Before 313, Christians in the Roman Empire were persecuted again and again because they did not worship the Roman gods. The Milan agreement gave them freedom of religion.
65413.m: Before 313, Christians were persecuted in the Roman Empire.

65414.q: Who called the Council of Nicaea?
65414.e: The emperor wanted to secure the unity of the Church and so of the empire. He invited the bishops and paid for their journey.
65414.m: Emperor Constantine called the Council of Nicaea.

65415.e: At a council, bishops discuss important questions of faith. At Nicaea in 325, it was mainly about the teaching of the priest Arius.
65415.m: A council is a meeting of bishops.

65416.q: What did the Council of Nicaea decide about the relationship between God the Father and the Son?
a: The Son is of the same substance as the Father
The Son is only a human being
The Son is below the Father
65416.e: The council used the Greek word “homoousios”, which means of the same substance. With this it rejected the opposing teaching that the Son had been created.
65416.m: At Nicaea, the Son was declared to be of the same substance as the Father.

65417.q: In which present-day country is the city of Nicaea?
65417.e: Nicaea was in Asia Minor near Constantinople. Today it is the small town of Iznik in Turkey.

65418.q: What number ecumenical council is the Council of Nicaea counted as?
65418.e: Ecumenical means that bishops came from the whole Church of that time. Nicaea was the first such meeting and is recognised by almost all churches.
65418.m: Nicaea was the first ecumenical council.

65419.q: Roughly how many bishops took part in the Council of Nicaea?
65419.e: Tradition names 318 bishops; other sources a few fewer. Most came from the east of the empire.
65419.m: About 300 bishops took part in the Council of Nicaea.

65420.q: The date of which Christian festival was standardised at the Council of Nicaea?
a: The date of All Saints' Day
The date of the Day of Prayer
65420.e: The council wanted all Christians to celebrate Easter on the same Sunday. Today the rule is: Easter is the Sunday after the first full moon of spring.
65420.m: The Council of Nicaea dealt with the date of Easter.

65421.q: What happened to the teaching of Arius at the Council of Nicaea?
a: It became binding for all churches
It was not discussed at all
It was written into the creed
65421.e: The council rejected the teaching that the Son of God was created. An important opponent of Arius was Athanasius of Alexandria.
65421.m: The teaching of Arius was rejected at Nicaea.

65422.q: What is the creed called after its first Latin word?
65422.e: In Latin the creed begins with “Credo”, which means “I believe”. That is why it is often called that.

65423.q: With which words does the creed begin in English?
a: Glory to God in the highest
65423.e: The creed begins with “I believe in God, the Father almighty”. In it Christians say what they believe.
65423.m: The creed begins with “I believe in God”.

65424.q: What does an old legend say about how the Apostles' Creed came about?
a: Each of the twelve apostles added one sentence
An angel brought it to Rome
65424.e: The legend explains the name Apostles' Creed. In fact it developed from an old Roman baptismal creed.
65424.m: According to legend, the twelve apostles wrote the Apostles' Creed.

65425.q: According to the creed, in which three persons of God do Christians believe?
65425.e: The creed is divided into three parts. This teaching of one God in three persons is called the Trinity.
65425.m: The creed speaks of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

65426.q: Which Roman governor is named in the creed?
65426.e: The creed says that Jesus suffered “under Pontius Pilate”. This anchors the events in history.
65426.m: Pontius Pilate is named in the creed.

65427.q: At which ceremony did the early Christians say a creed especially often?
65427.e: Anyone being baptised first declared their faith. Many creeds developed from such baptismal questions.
65427.m: Creeds were said at baptism from early on.

65428.q: Which two great parts of the Church separated in 1054?
65428.e: In 1054 the Church in the East, centred on Constantinople, and the Church in the West, centred on Rome, separated. One point of dispute was a word in the creed.
65428.m: In 1054 the Eastern and Western Churches separated.

a: It sums up what Christians believe
It tells the history of Switzerland
65429.e: A creed says in short sentences what is important in the Christian faith. It is also called a symbolum, which means sign of recognition.
65429.m: A creed sums up the Christian faith.

65430.q: In which language was the Nicene Creed originally written?
65430.e: Most of the bishops came from the Greek-speaking East. Only later was it translated into Latin.
65430.m: The Nicene Creed was written in Greek.

65431.q: Which religion did Emperor Theodosius make the state religion of the Roman Empire in 380?
65431.e: In 380 Theodosius decreed that all peoples should accept the Christian faith. With this, Christianity became the state religion.
65431.m: From 380, Christianity was the state religion.

65432.q: Theodosius issued an edict in 380. What is an edict?
a: A decree or order from a ruler
65432.e: With an edict, a ruler proclaimed a law. The edict of 380 is called “Cunctos populos” after its first words.
65432.m: An edict is a decree from a ruler.

65433.q: What did Theodosius ban in 391 and 392?
a: The sacrifices and cults of the old gods
65433.e: Theodosius banned sacrifices to the Roman gods and closed temples. The old cults thus lost their protection.

65434.q: After the edict of 380, what were Christians called who believed differently from the state church?
65434.e: The edict laid down what the right faith was. Anyone who believed differently was regarded as a heretic and could be punished.
65434.m: Anyone who believed differently was regarded as a heretic.

65435.q: What happened to the Roman Empire after Theodosius died in 395?
a: It was finally divided into West and East
It was conquered by Germanic peoples
65435.e: Theodosius was the last emperor to rule the whole empire. After him, his sons ruled separately.
65435.m: After Theodosius, the empire was finally divided.

65436.q: How many of Theodosius's sons shared the Roman Empire after his death?
65436.e: Honorius got the West, his brother Arcadius the East. Both were still young when their father died.
65436.m: Two sons shared the empire after Theodosius.

65437.q: What did Bishop Ambrose of Milan demand of Emperor Theodosius after a massacre?
a: That he step down as emperor
65437.e: After an uprising, Theodosius had thousands killed in Thessalonica in 390. Ambrose excluded him from church services until he did penance.
65437.m: Ambrose forced Emperor Theodosius to do penance.

65438.q: According to the traditional view, which ancient sporting games ended under Theodosius?
65438.e: It is traditionally assumed that the ancient Olympic Games ended around 393 as part of his bans. The exact end is disputed among historians.
65438.m: The ancient Olympic Games probably ended under Theodosius.

65439.q: Which province of the Roman Empire did Theodosius come from?
65439.e: Theodosius was born around 347 in Hispania, present-day Spain. He came from a family of officers.

65440.q: Who wrote the Rule of St Benedict for life in a monastery?
65440.e: Benedict of Nursia wrote the rule for his community of monks. It became the most important monastic rule in the West.
65440.m: Benedict of Nursia gave monks their best-known rule.

65441.q: Which Latin motto is often linked with the Rule of St Benedict?
65441.e: “Ora et labora” means “Pray and work”. The motto sums up the daily routine of the Benedictines, even though it is not written word for word in the rule.
65441.m: Benedictines are meant to pray and work.

65442.q: In which century was the Rule of St Benedict written?
65442.e: The rule was written around AD 540. That makes it almost 1500 years old.
65442.m: The Rule of St Benedict dates from the 6th century.

65443.q: Which monastery in Italy did Benedict found around 529?
65443.e: Benedict founded the monastery of Montecassino between Rome and Naples. He probably also wrote his rule there.
65443.m: Montecassino is the mother house of the Benedictines.

65445.q: What does the Rule of St Benedict set out?
a: The daily routine and life together of the monks
65445.e: The rule is divided into 73 chapters. It organises prayer, work, eating, sleeping and living together in the monastery.
65445.m: The Rule of St Benedict organises life in the monastery.

65447.q: Which well-known monastery in the canton of Schwyz belongs to the Benedictine order?
65447.e: Einsiedeln Abbey is a Benedictine abbey and an important place of pilgrimage with the Black Madonna.
65447.m: Einsiedeln is a Benedictine monastery in the canton of Schwyz.

65448.q: What title is Boniface known by?
65448.e: In the 8th century, Boniface spread Christianity in Germanic lands. That is why he is called the “Apostle of the Germans”.
65448.m: Boniface is regarded as the Apostle of the Germans.

65449.q: Which country did Boniface come from?
65449.e: Boniface was born around 673 in the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Wessex in southern England. He came to the Continent as a missionary.

65450.q: Who gave the missionary Winfrid the name Boniface?
65450.e: Boniface was first called Winfrid. The Pope in Rome gave him the name Boniface, “the one who does good”.
65450.m: The Pope gave Winfrid the name Boniface.

65451.q: Which tree, sacred to the god Donar (Thor), did Boniface have cut down near Geismar?
65451.e: Around 723 he felled Donar's Oak to show that the old god was powerless. A chapel is said to have been built from the wood.

a: He was killed on a missionary journey
He died at a great age in a monastery
65452.e: Boniface was killed by opponents near Dokkum in Frisia, in the north of the present-day Netherlands. That is why he is regarded as a martyr.

65453.q: What did Boniface and his followers found in Germania that became centres of faith?
65453.e: Boniface founded monasteries such as Fulda, where he is also buried. The monasteries became places of faith and learning.
65453.m: Boniface founded monasteries such as Fulda.

65454.q: Which office did Boniface hold later in his life?
65454.e: Boniface became a missionary archbishop and from 746 Bishop of Mainz. He reorganised the Church in the Frankish kingdom.

65455.q: Boniface's feast day is 5 June. What happened on this day?
65455.e: A saint's feast day is usually the day of their death. Boniface was killed on 5 June 754 or 755.
65455.m: A saint's feast day is often the day they died.

65456.q: From which period does the Plan of St Gall date?
65456.e: The plan was made around 825, in the early Middle Ages at the time of the Carolingians.
65456.m: The monastery plan dates from the Middle Ages.

65457.q: Was the Abbey of St Gallen built exactly according to the famous monastery plan?
a: No, the plan was more of an ideal picture
No, the plan shows a castle
65457.e: The plan shows an ideal monastery. But the Abbey of St Gallen was not built exactly like this.
65457.m: The monastery plan shows an ideal monastery.

65458.q: Who lived in a monastery like the one shown on the Plan of St Gall?
65458.e: Monks lived in the monastery. They prayed, worked, taught and cared for the sick.

65459.q: On what material is the Plan of St Gall drawn?
65459.e: The plan is made of five pieces of parchment sewn together. It is about 112 cm high and 77.5 cm wide.
65459.m: The monastery plan is drawn on parchment.

65460.q: Where is the monastery plan kept today?
a: In the Abbey Library of St Gallen
In the Swiss National Museum in Zurich
65460.e: The plan is one of the treasures of the Abbey Library of St Gallen. Because the inks are sensitive to light, the original is shown only rarely and briefly.
65460.m: The monastery plan is in the Abbey Library of St Gallen.

65461.q: What does the Plan of St Gall show?
65461.e: It shows a whole monastery complex with a church, school, hospital, workshops, stables and gardens. But the monastery was not built exactly according to this plan.
65461.m: The monastery plan shows a whole monastery complex.

65462.q: What is the Plan of St Gall especially famous for?
a: Earliest drawing of a monastery from the Middle Ages
65462.e: It is regarded as the earliest drawn picture of a monastery complex from the Middle Ages. That makes it unique for research.
65462.m: The monastery plan is the earliest monastery drawing of the Middle Ages.

65463.q: What is happening today near Messkirch based on the Plan of St Gall?
a: A monastery is being built with medieval tools
A theme park with roller coasters is being built
65463.e: On the Campus Galli building site, craftspeople have been working only with medieval tools since 2013. Visitors can watch.
65463.m: At Campus Galli, a monastery is being built according to the plan.

65465.q: What is the writing room in a medieval monastery called?
