66351.e: In 2016 the association reported about 3,700 members. That was less than 1 per cent of Muslims in Switzerland.
66351.m: The Islamic Central Council of Switzerland is a small, controversial group.

66352.q: How are most mosque associations in Switzerland legally organised?
66352.e: Muslim communities are mostly organised under private law as associations. That is why they cannot collect church taxes.
66352.m: Mosque associations in Switzerland are mostly private associations.

66353.q: In which body have representatives of Christians, Jews and Muslims met to discuss matters together since 2006?
66353.e: The Swiss Council of Religions includes leaders of the major religious communities, among them representatives of Muslim umbrella organisations.
66353.m: In the Council of Religions, Christians, Jews and Muslims talk to each other.

66354.q: How are most mosque associations in Switzerland organised?
66354.e: There are, for example, Albanian, Bosnian, Turkish and Arab mosque associations. They often keep close ties with the country of origin.
66354.m: Many mosque associations are organised by origin and language.

66355.q: Which organisation was founded in Zurich in 2004 and works for a liberal Islam?
66355.e: The Forum for a Progressive Islam stands for a liberal interpretation of the religion and works for equal rights.
66355.m: The Forum for a Progressive Islam stands for a liberal Islam.

66356.q: An umbrella organisation brings together Islamic communities in Eastern Switzerland and which neighbouring country?
66356.e: The umbrella organisation of Islamic communities of Eastern Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein was founded in 2003.
66356.m: Muslims in Eastern Switzerland and Liechtenstein share an umbrella organisation.

66357.e: Sufis seek an inner, personal closeness to God, for example through prayer, music and meditation.
66357.m: Sufism is the mysticism of Islam.

66358.q: The word “Sufi” is usually traced back to the Arabic word for which material?
66358.e: Early Sufis wore simple robes of rough wool, “suf” in Arabic. This showed their modesty.
66358.m: The word Sufi probably comes from “wool”.

66359.q: What did the Persian word “dervish” originally mean?
66359.e: A dervish is a member of a Sufi order. The word means “poor” or “beggar” and stands for a simple life.

66360.q: How do Sufis often remember God?
a: They repeat short prayers again and again
They stay silent for a whole year
66360.e: Sufis repeat names of God or short prayers, often together and in rhythm. This is called dhikr.
66360.m: Dhikr is remembering God through repetition.

66361.e: Rumi lived in the 13th century and wrote famous poems about love for God. Many people visit his tomb in Konya in Turkey.
66361.m: Rumi was a famous Sufi poet.

66362.q: What do the dervishes do during their famous ceremony to music?
66362.e: The ceremony is called Sema and is a prayer in movement. The dervishes spin around themselves and at the same time move in a circle.
66362.m: During the Sema the dervishes spin in prayer.

66363.q: What colour is the robe of the whirling dervishes?
66363.e: The whirling dervishes wear a white robe, a black cloak and a tall hat. They belong to the Mevlevi order.
66363.m: The whirling dervishes wear a white robe.

66364.q: What is the tall felt hat of the whirling dervishes meant to represent?
66364.e: The hat stands for the gravestone and the black cloak for the grave. The white robe recalls the burial shroud.
66364.m: The dervishes' tall hat stands for a gravestone.

66365.q: What kind of instrument is the ney, which is played at dervish ceremonies?
66365.e: The ney is an end-blown flute made of reed. Its sound is seen as the soul's longing for God.
66365.m: The ney is a reed flute of the Sufis.

66366.q: What is the meeting house of the Alevis called?
66366.e: The Alevis' services take place in the cemevi. Most Alevis do not pray in mosques.

66367.q: What is part of the Alevi religious service, the cem?
66367.e: At the cem, poems are recited, music is played and there is ritual dancing. Women and men celebrate together.
66367.m: The Alevi religious service is called the cem.

66368.q: Who celebrates the religious service together among the Alevis?
66368.e: Among the Alevis, women and men pray together in the same room. This makes them different from many other Muslim communities.
66368.m: Among Alevis, women and men celebrate together.

66369.q: Alevis call their spiritual leader “dede”. What does this word mean?
66369.e: A dede leads the cem and advises the community. The word means “grandfather” and shows respect for his experience.
66369.m: The spiritual leader of the Alevis is called the dede.

66370.q: Which person do Alevis honour especially?
66370.e: Ali was the son-in-law and cousin of the Prophet Muhammad. Alevis often name him together with God and Muhammad.

66371.q: Which string instrument is very important in Alevi worship?
66371.e: The saz, also called bağlama, is a long-necked lute. Many Alevis see their music as part of prayer.
66371.m: The saz is the sacred instrument of the Alevis.

66372.q: For how many days do many Alevis fast in the month of Muharrem?
66372.e: The twelve days of fasting recall the twelve imams. They end with the Aşure festival, when a sweet dish is shared.
66372.m: Many Alevis fast for twelve days in Muharrem.

66373.q: Roughly what share of Turkey's population are Alevis, according to estimates?
66373.e: Estimates suggest about 15 per cent, which is more than 12 million people. There are no exact figures.
66373.m: The Alevis are a large minority in Turkey.

66374.q: Which canton recognised two Alevi communities in 2012 as the first non-Christian and non-Jewish religious community in Switzerland?
66374.e: The Grand Council of Basel-Stadt granted cantonal recognition in October 2012.
66374.m: Basel-Stadt officially recognised the Alevis in 2012.

66375.e: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad founded the movement in British India. Its name comes from his name.
66375.m: The Ahmadiyya goes back to Mirza Ghulam Ahmad.

66376.q: Roughly when did the Ahmadiyya movement begin?
66376.e: On 23 March 1889 the first followers swore an oath of loyalty to the founder in Ludhiana. So the Ahmadiyya is a young movement in Islam.

66377.q: In which area did the Ahmadiyya begin?
66377.e: The movement began in the Punjab, which then belonged to British India. Today this area is in India and Pakistan.
66377.m: The Ahmadiyya comes from the Punjab in British India.

66378.q: What is the well-known motto of the Ahmadiyya?
a: Love for all, hatred for none
One for all, all for one
66378.e: Ahmadiyya communities often display this motto on mosques and at events.
66378.m: The motto of the Ahmadiyya is “Love for all, hatred for none”.

66379.q: In which country does the leadership of the largest Ahmadiyya community have its headquarters today?
66379.e: Because the Ahmadiyya were persecuted in Pakistan, the leadership moved to London in 1984. Since 2019 the headquarters have been in Tilford in southern England.
66379.m: The leadership of the Ahmadiyya is based in the United Kingdom.

66380.q: What did Pakistan decide about the Ahmadiyya in 1974?
a: They are not considered Muslims there
They were given their own provinces
66380.e: In 1974 a change to the constitution declared the Ahmadis a non-Muslim minority. Since then they have faced heavy discrimination there.
66380.m: In Pakistan, Ahmadis have not been considered Muslims since 1974.

66381.q: What title does the head of the largest Ahmadiyya community hold?
66381.e: After the founder's death in 1908, the community chose a successor with the title caliph. There have been five caliphs so far.
66381.m: The head of the Ahmadiyya is called the caliph.

66382.q: How is the head of the largest Ahmadiyya community chosen?
a: They are elected by a body of the community
They are appointed by the King of England
They are chosen by drawing lots
They always inherit the office from their father
66382.e: After a caliph dies, an electoral body of the community chooses the successor. This is how Mirza Masroor Ahmad was elected in 2003.
66382.m: The head of the Ahmadiyya is elected.

66383.q: Who did the founder of the Ahmadiyya believe himself to be?
66383.e: The founder saw himself as the promised Messiah and Mahdi. Most other Muslims reject this teaching.
66383.m: The founder of the Ahmadiyya saw himself as the promised Messiah.

66384.q: What is special about the Mahmud Mosque in Zurich, which opened in 1963?
a: It is seen as the first purpose-built mosque in Switzerland.
It is the largest mosque in Europe.
It stands on a mountain top.
It used to be a church.
66384.e: The Mahmud Mosque opened in 1963. It is seen as the first mosque in Switzerland that was built specially as a mosque.

66385.q: In which city is the Mahmud Mosque?
66385.e: The Mahmud Mosque stands in the largest city in Switzerland and can be recognised from far away by its minaret.
66385.m: The Mahmud Mosque is in Zurich.

66386.q: How can you recognise the Mahmud Mosque in Zurich from far away?
66386.e: The Mahmud Mosque stands on Forchstrasse in Zurich. Its slender minaret can be seen from far away.
66386.m: The Mahmud Mosque has a minaret.

66387.q: The Ahmadiyya had the Mahmud Mosque in Zurich built. What is the Ahmadiyya?
66387.e: Missionaries of the Muslim Ahmadiyya community came to Switzerland in 1946. The mosque is still their centre in Switzerland today.
66387.m: The Mahmud Mosque belongs to the Ahmadiyya.

66388.q: What makes the Mahmud Mosque in Zurich special?
a: It is seen as the first purpose-built mosque in Switzerland
It is the largest mosque in Europe
It stands on a mountain top
66388.e: Before that, Muslims in Switzerland only prayed in converted rooms. The Mahmud Mosque was the first building in Switzerland built specially as a mosque.
66388.m: The Mahmud Mosque is seen as the first mosque in Switzerland.

66389.q: What is on top of the minaret of the Mahmud Mosque?
66389.e: There is a crescent moon on the minaret of the Mahmud Mosque. It is a well-known symbol of Islam.
66389.m: There is a crescent moon on the minaret of the Mahmud Mosque.

66390.q: Is the call to prayer made from the minaret of the Mahmud Mosque?
a: No, there is no call to prayer
66390.e: There is a crescent moon on the minaret, but it is not used for the call to prayer. It is mainly a sign that makes the mosque recognisable.
66390.m: No call to prayer comes from the minaret of the Mahmud Mosque.

66392.q: What makes the Mahmud Mosque recognisable from far away?
66392.e: The Mahmud Mosque has a minaret, a slender tower. That makes it easy to recognise as a mosque.
66392.m: You can recognise the Mahmud Mosque by its minaret.

66393.q: In which month of our calendar did Ramadan begin in 2026?
66393.e: Ramadan 2026 began around 18 February. Because it starts earlier every year, it will fall in winter in the next few years.

66394.q: What is the meal called that breaks the fast in the evening?
66394.e: Iftar is often celebrated with family and friends. Traditionally people start with dates and water.
66394.m: Iftar breaks the fast in the evening.

66395.q: What is the meal called that people who are fasting eat very early in the morning?
66395.e: Suhoor is eaten before the day of fasting begins. It is meant to give strength for the whole day.
66395.m: Suhoor is the early morning meal during Ramadan.

66396.q: Why does Ramadan begin about eleven days earlier each year?
66396.e: The Islamic year follows the moon and has only about 354 days. That is why Ramadan moves through all the seasons.
66396.m: Ramadan moves because the Islamic calendar is a lunar calendar.

66397.q: Do young children have to fast during Ramadan?
a: No, they do not have to
66397.e: The duty to fast applies only to teenagers and adults. Some children practise voluntarily on single days or half days.
66397.m: Young children do not have to fast during Ramadan.

66398.q: What applies during Ramadan to people who are ill?
a: They do not have to fast
They must fast twice as much
66398.e: People who are ill, people who are travelling and people for whom fasting is harmful do not have to fast. Those who can make up the days later.
66398.m: If you are ill, you do not have to fast during Ramadan.

66399.q: In many cantons, what applies to Muslim schoolchildren on major Islamic holidays?
a: They can be given the day off
The whole school has a day off
66399.e: Many cantons allow pupils to miss lessons on major religious holidays. Parents usually have to ask the school in advance.
66399.m: In many cantons you can get the day off school on major religious holidays.

66400.q: What is the special night in Ramadan called when, according to Islamic tradition, the first verses of the Quran were revealed?
66400.e: The Night of Power, Laylat al-Qadr in Arabic, is usually marked in one of the last ten nights of Ramadan. Many Muslims pray for an especially long time on this night.
66400.m: According to Islamic tradition, the revelation of the Quran began on the Night of Power.

66401.q: How many days does Ramadan last?
66401.e: A month in the Islamic calendar has 29 or 30 days. That is why the month of fasting, Ramadan, also lasts that long.

66402.q: In which direction are Muslim graves aligned?
66402.e: The dead are buried so that their face points towards Mecca. From Switzerland, Mecca lies to the south-east.

66403.q: What is a Muslim burial section in a Swiss cemetery?
a: An area where Muslims are buried according to their rules
A separate cemetery only for imams
66403.e: In Muslim burial sections the dead can be buried according to Islamic tradition. The first one was created in Geneva in 1978.
66403.m: Muslim burial sections make burials according to Islamic tradition possible.

66404.q: Why do some Swiss cemeteries have their own Muslim burial sections?
a: So that the graves can face Mecca
So that the graves are larger
So that no flowers grow there
So that they are closer to the church
66404.e: In ordinary cemeteries the graves often face a different way. In Muslim burial sections the dead lie with their face towards Mecca.
66404.m: Muslim burial sections make graves facing Mecca possible.

66405.q: According to Muslim tradition, what happens to the dead before burial?
a: They are made up with cosmetics
66405.e: Before the funeral the dead person is ritually washed and wrapped in a white cloth. Then they should be buried quickly.
66405.m: The dead are washed before a Muslim burial.

66406.q: According to Muslim tradition, what are the dead buried in?
a: In a wooden box with glass
66406.e: Traditionally the body is only wrapped in a white cloth. In Switzerland, however, many Muslims accept a coffin.
66406.m: Traditionally Muslims are buried in a shroud.

66407.q: Which type of burial does Islam reject?
66407.e: In Islam the body is not burned but laid to rest in the earth.
66407.m: Muslims are not cremated but buried.

66408.q: According to Muslim tradition, how quickly should a burial take place?
a: Within one or two days if possible
66408.e: First the dead person is ritually washed, then they should be buried quickly.
66408.m: Muslims are buried as soon as possible after death.

66409.q: Which common rule in Swiss cemeteries goes against the Muslim idea that a grave should rest for ever?
a: Graves are cleared after a few decades
Graves must be made of concrete
66409.e: In many Swiss cemeteries a grave is cleared after about 20 to 25 years. According to Islamic belief, however, a grave should not be removed.
66409.m: The limited resting time of graves is a challenge for Muslim burials.

66410.q: Who is usually responsible for cemeteries in Switzerland?
66410.e: In Switzerland cemeteries are usually run by the municipalities. So they also decide about Muslim burial sections.
66410.m: In Switzerland the municipalities are usually responsible for cemeteries.

66411.q: According to the Bible, which city in Mesopotamia did Abraham come from?
66411.e: According to the Book of Genesis, Abraham set out with his family from Ur of the Chaldeans. Ur lay in the south of Mesopotamia, in what is now Iraq.
66411.m: Abraham came from the city of Ur in Mesopotamia.

66412.q: Which land did Abraham move to after God's call?
66412.e: God promised Abraham the land of Canaan for his descendants. That is why Canaan is known as the “Promised Land”.
66412.m: Abraham moved to the Promised Land of Canaan.

66413.q: What was the name of Abraham's wife?
66413.e: Sarah was Abraham's wife and Isaac's mother. She is seen as one of the matriarchs of Israel.

66414.q: What was the name of Isaac's wife?
66414.e: Abraham's servant brought Rebecca from Abraham's relatives to be Isaac's wife. She is one of the four matriarchs.

66415.q: What did Esau sell his birthright to his brother Jacob for?
66415.e: Esau came back hungry from hunting and swapped his birthright for a dish of lentils. That is what the Book of Genesis tells.
66415.m: Esau gave up his birthright for a bowl of lentil stew.

66416.q: Which new name did Jacob receive after his night-time struggle at the river Jabbok?
66416.e: After the struggle with a mysterious opponent, Jacob was given the name Israel. The term “people of Israel” comes from this name.
66416.m: Jacob was given the name Israel.

66417.q: What did Jacob dream about at Bethel?
66417.e: In his dream Jacob saw a ladder with angels going up and down it. He called the place Bethel, which means “house of God”.
66417.m: At Bethel Jacob dreamt of the ladder to heaven.

66418.q: In which city is the Cave of Machpelah, the tomb of the patriarchs?
66418.e: According to the Bible, Abraham bought the Cave of Machpelah near Hebron as a burial place. Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are said to be buried there with their wives.
66418.m: The patriarchs were buried in the Cave of Machpelah in Hebron.

66419.q: According to the Bible, who are the twelve tribes of Israel descended from?
66419.e: Jacob had twelve sons. Each of them is seen as the forefather of one of the twelve tribes.
66419.m: The twelve tribes go back to the twelve sons of Jacob.

66420.q: Which tribe received no land of its own because it served at the sanctuary?
66420.e: The Levites were in charge of worship and were given individual towns instead of land. The priests also came from them.
66420.m: The tribe of Levi served at the sanctuary and had no land of its own.

66421.q: Which tribe does the word “Jews” come from?
66421.e: The southern kingdom was called “Judah” after the tribe of Judah. Its inhabitants were called Judeans, and from this came the word “Jews”.
66421.m: The word “Jews” comes from the tribe of Judah.

66422.q: Which son of Jacob was sold to Egypt by his brothers?
66422.e: Joseph was Jacob's favourite son. His jealous brothers sold him to Egypt. His sons Ephraim and Manasseh later became the forefathers of their own tribes.
66422.m: Joseph was sold to Egypt by his brothers.

66423.q: What are the tribes of the northern kingdom that disappeared after the Assyrian conquest called?
66423.e: Around 722 BC the Assyrians conquered the northern kingdom of Israel and carried many people away. Since then these tribes have been seen as lost.
66423.m: The ten tribes of the northern kingdom are seen as lost.

66424.q: Which tribe did King David come from?
66424.e: David came from Bethlehem in the land of the tribe of Judah. His family then ruled the kingdom of Judah for a long time.
66424.m: King David belonged to the tribe of Judah.

66425.q: Which tribe did Saul, the first king of Israel, come from?
66425.e: Saul was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin. He was anointed the first king by the prophet Samuel.
66425.m: Saul, the first king of Israel, came from the tribe of Benjamin.

66426.q: Which three parts make up the word “Tanakh”?
66426.e: Tanakh is a made-up word from the first letters T, N and K: Torah, Nevi'im (Prophets) and Ketuvim (Writings).
66426.m: The Tanakh is made up of the Torah, the Prophets and the Writings.

66427.e: The Tanakh is the Holy Scripture of Judaism. It is made up of the Torah, the Prophets and the Writings.
66427.m: The Tanakh is the Holy Scripture of Judaism.

66428.q: Which part of the Tanakh do the Psalms belong to?
66428.e: The Psalms are in the third part, the Ketuvim or Writings. Proverbs and the Book of Ruth also belong to it.
66428.m: The Psalms belong to the Writings of the Tanakh.

66429.q: Is the Tanakh a single book?
a: No, it is a collection of many books
Yes, it is a single letter
Yes, it is a single song
No, it is a collection of pictures
66429.e: The Tanakh is a collection of many books, such as the five books of Moses, the Prophets and the Psalms. According to Jewish counting there are 24 books.
66429.m: The Tanakh is a collection of many books.

66430.q: What do Christians call the part of their Bible that matches the Tanakh?
66430.e: Christians took over the scriptures of the Tanakh and call them the Old Testament. The order of the books is partly different there.
66430.m: The Tanakh matches the Christian Old Testament.

66431.q: In which language is almost all of the Tanakh written?
66431.e: The Tanakh is written almost entirely in Hebrew. Only a few chapters, for example in Daniel and Ezra, are in Aramaic.
66431.m: The Tanakh is written almost entirely in Hebrew.

66432.q: Where were very old scrolls with texts of the Tanakh found from 1947 onwards?
66432.e: From 1947 onwards the Dead Sea Scrolls were discovered in caves near Qumran by the Dead Sea. They are over 2000 years old.
66432.m: The Dead Sea Scrolls were found near Qumran.

66433.q: Which part of the Tanakh does the Book of Isaiah belong to?
66433.e: Isaiah is seen as one of the major prophets. That is why his book is in the second part of the Tanakh, the Nevi'im.
66433.m: The Book of Isaiah belongs to the Prophets.

66434.q: What is the first book of the Torah, which begins with the creation of the world, called?
66434.e: The first book of Moses is called Genesis, in Hebrew Bereshit, which means “In the beginning”. It tells the story from the creation to Joseph in Egypt.
66434.m: The Torah begins with the Book of Genesis.

66435.q: How many books make up the Torah?
66435.e: The Torah is made up of the five books of Moses: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy.
66435.m: The Torah is made up of the five books of Moses.

66436.q: Which well-known commandments are in the Torah?
66436.e: The Ten Commandments are in the Torah, in the second and fifth books of Moses. According to Jewish tradition, the Torah contains as many as 613 commandments and prohibitions in total.
66436.m: The Ten Commandments are in the Torah.

66437.q: What does the Hebrew word “Torah” mean?
66437.e: Torah means roughly “instruction” or “teaching” in English. It refers to the teaching that God gave to the people of Israel.
66437.m: The word Torah means instruction or teaching.

66438.q: What are the five books of Moses called, using a Greek word?
66438.e: Pentateuch comes from Greek and means roughly “five vessels” or “five books”. It refers to the five books of Moses.
66438.m: Pentateuch is the Greek name for the five books of Moses.

66440.q: Which festival celebrates the end and the new beginning of the yearly Torah reading?
66440.e: The Torah is read through completely once a year in weekly portions. On Simchat Torah, “Joy of the Torah”, the end is read and the reading starts again straight away from the beginning.
66440.m: On Simchat Torah the Torah reading starts again from the beginning.

66441.q: How often is the whole Torah read aloud in the synagogue?
a: Once a year, in weekly portions
66441.e: The Torah is divided into 54 weekly portions. One of them is read on Shabbat each week, so the whole Torah is read in a year.
66441.m: The whole Torah is read aloud once every year.

a: A collection of Jewish teachings and interpretations
A part of the New Testament
66442.e: The Talmud is a very large work of Judaism. In it scholars explain and discuss the Torah and the rules for daily life.
66442.m: The Talmud collects Jewish teachings and interpretations of the Torah.

66443.e: Many rabbis, that is Jewish scholars, worked on the Talmud over several centuries. Their discussions were collected and written down.
66443.m: The Talmud is the work of many Jewish scholars.

66444.q: What is the teaching called that was written down in the Talmud?
66444.e: According to Jewish belief, Moses received an oral Torah as well as the written one. It was passed on by word of mouth for a long time and later written down in the Mishnah and Talmud.
66444.m: The Talmud records the Oral Torah in writing.

66445.q: Which is older: the Torah or the Talmud?
a: Both are exactly the same age
Neither, both are only 100 years old
66445.e: The Torah is much older. The Talmud came later: from about AD 200 scholars wrote down their explanations of the Torah.
66445.m: The Talmud is younger than the Torah and explains it.

a: Very big, it fills many thick volumes
It fits on a single sheet
66446.e: The Talmud is huge. A printed edition often has about 20 thick volumes with thousands of pages.
66446.m: The Talmud is a very large work.

66447.q: What does Jewish religious law regulate, for example?
a: What you may eat and what is allowed on Shabbat
Which party you should vote for
66447.e: Jewish religious law is called halakha. It comes from the Torah and Talmud and regulates daily life, from prayer to food to Shabbat.
66447.m: Jewish religious law regulates food, prayer and Shabbat.

66448.q: How do Jewish pupils often study the Talmud?
a: Only with videos on the computer
Only by copying from the blackboard
66448.e: The Talmud is often studied in pairs: you read the text and discuss it. That is why in a Talmud school, the yeshiva, you hear many voices at the same time.
66448.m: The Talmud is often studied in pairs through discussion.

66449.q: What is often written around the main text on a page of the Talmud?
66449.e: On a page of the Talmud the main text is in the middle. Around it are commentaries by famous scholars, for example by Rashi from France.
66449.m: Explanations by scholars surround the Talmud text.

66450.q: What did the word “kosher” originally mean?
66450.e: Kosher comes from the Hebrew “kasher” and means “fit” or “suitable”. It refers to foods that are allowed according to the rules.

66451.q: Which two features must a land animal have to be kosher?
a: Split hooves and chewing the cud
66451.e: According to the Torah, only mammals that have split hooves and chew the cud are allowed. Cattle, sheep and goats meet both conditions.
66451.m: Kosher land animals have split hooves and chew the cud.

66452.q: Which two features must a water animal have to be kosher?
66452.e: Only water animals with fins and scales are allowed. That is why salmon and trout are kosher, but prawns and mussels are not.
66452.m: Kosher fish have fins and scales.

66453.q: According to the food laws, which drink is only kosher if it was made under Jewish supervision?
66453.e: Wine and grape juice are only considered kosher if they were made under Jewish supervision. One reason is that wine used to be used in sacrifices to other gods.
66453.m: Kosher wine is made under Jewish supervision.

66454.q: According to the food laws, which two food groups may not be eaten together?
66454.e: The Torah forbids cooking a young goat in its mother's milk. From this came the rule of keeping meat and dairy products strictly apart, often even with separate crockery.
66454.m: Meat and milk are kept apart in the kosher kitchen.

66455.q: In the kosher kitchen, which foods may be eaten with meat and also with milk?
66455.e: Eggs, fruit and vegetables are neither meat nor dairy. Such neutral foods are called parve.
66455.m: Parve foods may be eaten with meat and with milk.

66456.q: What is ritual slaughter according to the Jewish food laws called?
66456.e: In shechita the animal is killed with a very sharp knife so that the blood flows out. Consuming blood is forbidden in the Torah.

66457.q: How can you tell in a shop that a product is kosher?
a: By a mark of rabbinical supervision
66457.e: Such a seal of approval is called a hechsher. It confirms that the ingredients and production meet the Jewish food laws.
66457.m: A hechsher confirms that a product is kosher.

66458.q: What does “Rosh Hashanah” mean in English?
66458.e: Rosh means “head” and shanah means “year”. Rosh Hashanah is the Jewish New Year festival.
66458.m: Rosh Hashanah means head of the year.

66459.q: In which months of our calendar does Rosh Hashanah usually fall?
66459.e: Rosh Hashanah is at the beginning of the month of Tishri in the Jewish lunar calendar. In our calendar that is in September or early October.
66459.m: Rosh Hashanah is celebrated in September or October.

66460.q: Which Jewish year began at Rosh Hashanah in September 2026?
66460.e: According to tradition, the Jewish count of years begins with the creation of the world. In September 2026 the year 5787 began.
66460.m: In autumn 2026 the Jewish year 5787 began.

66461.q: Which holiday ends the Ten Days of Repentance that begin at Rosh Hashanah?
66461.e: Rosh Hashanah is on 1 Tishri, Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, on 10 Tishri. The days in between are called the Ten Days of Repentance.
66461.m: The Ten Days of Repentance end with Yom Kippur.

66462.q: In the Tashlich custom at Rosh Hashanah, what do people throw into flowing water?
66462.e: For Tashlich people go to a river or lake and throw breadcrumbs into the water. It is a sign of throwing away sins symbolically.
66462.m: For Tashlich people throw breadcrumbs into the water.

66463.q: With which wish do people greet each other at Rosh Hashanah?
66463.e: “Shanah tovah” means “good year”. People often say more fully “Shanah tovah u'metukah”, a good and sweet year.
66463.m: At Rosh Hashanah people wish each other “Shanah tovah”.

66464.q: What shape is the challah bread at Rosh Hashanah usually?
66464.e: At Rosh Hashanah the challah is baked round instead of as a long plait. The round shape stands for the cycle of the year.
66464.m: At Rosh Hashanah the challah is round.

66465.q: From which animal's horn may a shofar not be made?
66465.e: A shofar is usually made from a ram's horn. Cow horn is not allowed because it is a reminder of the Golden Calf.
66465.m: A shofar may not be made from a cow's horn.

66466.q: What does the tekiah, one of the sounds of the shofar, sound like?
66466.e: There are three kinds of sound when the shofar is blown: tekiah, shevarim and teruah. The tekiah is a long, steady note.
66466.m: The tekiah is the long note of the shofar.

66467.q: When is the shofar blown every weekday morning in many Jewish communities?
a: In the month before the Jewish New Year
66467.e: In the month of Elul before the New Year, many communities blow the shofar every morning. It is meant to remind people to repent.
66467.m: In the month before Rosh Hashanah the shofar sounds every morning.

66468.q: On which day is the shofar not blown, even if Rosh Hashanah falls on it?
66468.e: If the first day of Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat, the shofar is not blown. The rabbis wanted to stop anyone from carrying it around on the day of rest.
66468.m: The shofar is not blown on Shabbat.

66469.q: According to the Bible, outside which city did the Israelites blow the shofars until the walls collapsed?
66469.e: According to the Book of Joshua, the Israelites marched around Jericho for seven days. On the seventh day they blew the horns, and the walls fell.
66469.m: At Jericho the walls fell at the sound of the horns.

66470.q: Which story does the ram's horn of the shofar recall?
a: The ram sacrificed instead of Isaac
66470.e: Instead of his son Isaac, Abraham sacrificed a ram that had got caught in a thicket. The ram's horn recalls this story.
66470.m: The ram's horn recalls the ram that was sacrificed in Isaac's place.

66471.q: What does a member of the congregation call out to the shofar blower in the synagogue?
66471.e: The shofar blower is called the baal tokea, “master of blowing”. Another member of the congregation calls out to him the notes he should blow.
66471.m: The notes are called out to the shofar blower.

66472.e: Bat means “daughter” and mitzvah means “commandment”. With it a girl comes of religious age.
66472.m: Bat Mitzvah means daughter of the commandment.

66473.q: At what age do Jewish girls become Bat Mitzvah?
66473.e: According to Jewish law, girls come of religious age at 12 and boys only at 13. From then on the commandments apply to them as to adults.

66474.q: What is the matching ceremony for Jewish boys called?
66474.e: Bar is the Aramaic word for “son”. The Bar Mitzvah is the celebration of coming of religious age for boys.
66474.m: Jewish boys celebrate their Bar Mitzvah.

66475.q: What may a girl do at her Bat Mitzvah in liberal communities?
66475.e: In liberal communities girls read from the Torah scroll at their Bat Mitzvah, just like boys. In Orthodox communities it is usually celebrated differently, for example with a speech.
66475.m: In liberal communities the girl reads from the Torah at her Bat Mitzvah.

66476.q: When did the Bat Mitzvah begin as a public ceremony?
66476.e: The first public Bat Mitzvah in the USA took place in New York in 1922. The ceremony for boys is much older.
66476.m: As a ceremony, the Bat Mitzvah is a young custom.

66477.q: From which scripture does the girl often read at her Bat Mitzvah?
66477.e: The Torah is the five books of Moses. It is read from during the service, and at a Bat Mitzvah often by the person being celebrated.
66477.m: At a Bat Mitzvah there is a reading from the Torah.

66478.q: Does a girl become Bat Mitzvah even without a ceremony?
a: Yes, simply by reaching the age
66478.e: According to Jewish law, religious adulthood comes automatically with age. The ceremony is a lovely custom, but not a condition.
66478.m: You become Bat Mitzvah by age, even without a ceremony.

66479.q: Which king had the first Temple in Jerusalem built?
66479.e: According to the Bible, King Solomon, the son of David, built the first Temple. That is why it is also called Solomon's Temple.
66479.m: King Solomon built the first Temple in Jerusalem.

66480.q: Who destroyed the first Temple in 586 BC?
66480.e: The army of the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar II conquered Jerusalem and destroyed the Temple. Many people were taken away to Babylon.
66480.m: The Babylonians destroyed the first Temple.

66481.q: In which year did the Romans destroy the second Temple?
66481.e: In the Jewish War the Romans under Titus conquered Jerusalem and destroyed the Temple in the year 70. It was never rebuilt.
66481.m: The Romans destroyed the second Temple in the year 70.

66482.q: Which part of the old Temple complex in Jerusalem is an important place of prayer today?
66482.e: The Western Wall, also called the Wailing Wall, is part of the wall around the second Temple. Many Jews pray there and push notes with prayers into the cracks.
66482.m: The Western Wall is a remnant of the Temple complex in Jerusalem.

66483.q: What is the Western Wall a remnant of?
a: The retaining wall of the Temple Mount
66483.e: The Western Wall is part of the western retaining wall that Herod had built around the Temple Mount. It is the most important place of prayer in Judaism.
66483.m: The Western Wall is part of the wall around the Temple Mount.

66484.q: In which city is the Western Wall?
66484.e: The Western Wall, in Hebrew the Kotel, stands in the Old City of Jerusalem on the western side of the Temple Mount.
66484.m: The Western Wall is in Jerusalem.

66485.q: Where does the Wailing Wall get its name from?
a: From the mourning for the destroyed Temple
From complaints made in a court
From the wind that howls there
66485.e: For centuries Jews have prayed at this wall and mourned the destruction of the Temple. That is why Europeans called it the Wailing Wall.
66485.m: The Wailing Wall is named after the mourning for the destroyed Temple.

66486.q: Which building with a golden dome stands on the Temple Mount today?
a: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre
66486.e: The Dome of the Rock was built at the end of the 7th century. It stands on the Temple Mount, roughly where the Temple once stood.
66486.m: The Dome of the Rock stands on the Temple Mount today.

66487.q: What does the Greek word “diaspora” mean?
66487.e: Diaspora means “scattering”. It refers to Jews who live outside the land of Israel.

66488.q: In which Egyptian city did a particularly large Jewish community live in ancient times?
66488.e: A great many Jews lived in Alexandria in ancient times. From the 3rd century BC the Septuagint, the Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible, was made there.
66488.m: Alexandria had a large Jewish community in ancient times.

66489.q: What are Jews whose ancestors lived in Central and Eastern Europe called?
66489.e: Ashkenaz was the Hebrew name for Germany. The Ashkenazim first lived on the Rhine and later mainly in Eastern Europe.
66489.m: The Ashkenazim have their roots in Central and Eastern Europe.

66490.q: In which year were the Jews expelled from Spain?
66490.e: With the Alhambra Decree of 1492 all Jews had to leave Spain or be baptised. Many Sephardim moved to North Africa and the Ottoman Empire.
66490.m: In 1492 the Jews were expelled from Spain.

66491.q: Which language developed among the Jews of Central and Eastern Europe from Middle High German?
66491.e: Yiddish is based mainly on German, with Hebrew and Slavic words. It is written with Hebrew letters.
66491.m: Yiddish developed from Middle High German.

66492.q: In which country outside Israel do the most Jews live today?
66492.e: About 6 to 7 million Jews live in the USA (as of 2024), slightly fewer than in Israel. It is the largest Jewish community of the diaspora.
66492.m: The largest diaspora community lives in the USA.

66493.q: In which city was the first ghetto set up in 1516, after which all later ones are named?
66493.e: In Venice, from 1516 Jews had to live in a closed-off quarter. The word “ghetto” probably comes from a foundry that stood there.
66493.m: The word ghetto comes from Venice.

66494.q: What is the immigration of Jews from the diaspora to Israel called?
66494.e: Aliyah means “going up”. Since Israel was founded in 1948, millions of Jews from all over the world have immigrated.
66494.m: Immigration to Israel is called aliyah.

66495.q: How can you often recognise ultra-Orthodox Jewish men?
a: By dark clothes and a hat
66495.e: Ultra-Orthodox Jews are called Haredim in Hebrew, “those who fear God”. They live very strictly by religious law and often wear dark clothes.
66495.m: Ultra-Orthodox Jews often wear dark clothes.

66496.q: How do men and women sit in an Orthodox synagogue?
66496.e: In Orthodox synagogues men and women sit in separate areas. There is often a women's gallery or a partition called a mechitza.
66496.m: In Orthodox synagogues men and women sit separately.

66497.q: What do Orthodox Jews not do on Shabbat?
66497.e: On Shabbat, according to Jewish religious law, many kinds of work are forbidden, including making fire. That is why Orthodox Jews do not drive and do not use electrical devices.
66497.m: Orthodox Jews do not drive on Shabbat.

66498.q: How do Orthodox Jews understand the Torah?
a: As the word of God given at Sinai
As a collection of old fairy tales
As a history book of the Romans
66498.e: For Orthodox Judaism, God gave the Torah to Moses on Mount Sinai. That is why its commandments apply unchanged.
66498.m: For the Orthodox, the Torah is God's word from Sinai.

66499.q: In which country did Liberal Judaism begin in the 19th century?
66499.e: Reformers such as Abraham Geiger wanted to adapt Judaism to modern times. The movement began in Germany and later spread to the USA.

66500.q: What is allowed in liberal communities, unlike in Orthodox ones?
66500.e: In Liberal Judaism women and men have the same religious rights. That is why there are women rabbis.
66500.m: In liberal communities women can become rabbis.

66501.q: What did Regina Jonas from Berlin become in 1935, as the first woman in the world?
66501.e: Regina Jonas was ordained as a rabbi in Offenbach am Main in 1935. She was murdered in Auschwitz in 1944.
66501.m: Regina Jonas was the first woman rabbi in the world.

66502.q: In which Swiss city is the liberal Jewish community Or Chadasch?
66502.e: The name Or Chadasch means “new light”. It is one of the largest liberal Jewish communities in Switzerland.
66502.m: The liberal Jewish community in Zurich is called Or Chadasch.

66503.q: In which canton are Endingen and Lengnau?
66503.e: The two neighbouring villages are in the district of Zurzach in the canton of Aargau. They are among the most important places of Jewish history in Switzerland.
66503.m: Endingen and Lengnau are in the canton of Aargau.

66504.q: In which valley are Endingen and Lengnau?
66504.e: Endingen and Lengnau lie on the Surb, a tributary of the Aare. That is why people often speak of the “Surbtal Jews”.
66504.m: Endingen and Lengnau are in the Surbtal.

66505.q: What was special about Endingen and Lengnau from 1776?
a: Only there were Jews allowed to live in Switzerland
The only church in Aargau stood there
66505.e: From 1776 Jews in Switzerland only had the right to live in these two villages. But they were not allowed to do many jobs or own land.
66505.m: From 1776 Jews in Switzerland were only allowed to live in Endingen and Lengnau.

66506.q: What is special about the Jewish cemetery between Endingen and Lengnau?
a: It is the oldest existing one in Switzerland
It is the largest cemetery in Europe
It is on a mountain top
It is only open at night
66506.e: The cemetery was laid out around 1750 and is today the oldest Jewish cemetery in Switzerland that still exists. It is a protected monument.
66506.m: The oldest Jewish cemetery in Switzerland lies between Endingen and Lengnau.

66507.q: Where did the Jews from Endingen and Lengnau bury their dead before 1750?
a: On an island in the Rhine
66507.e: Before that they had to bury their dead on the “Judenäule”, a small island in the Rhine near Koblenz in Aargau. Floods often destroyed the graves there.
66507.m: Before 1750 the graves of the Jews from Endingen and Lengnau were on an island in the Rhine.

66508.q: What does the synagogue in Endingen have that synagogues hardly ever have?
a: A bell tower with a cross
66508.e: Endingen had no church with a tower, so the synagogue from 1852 carries the village clock. That is very unusual for a synagogue.
66508.m: The synagogue in Endingen carries the village clock.

66509.q: Which Jewish place of worship stands in Lengnau and in Endingen?
66509.e: Both villages have a synagogue from the 19th century. The synagogue in Lengnau was consecrated in 1847.
66509.m: There are synagogues in Endingen and Lengnau.

66510.q: From which year were Jews allowed to settle freely anywhere in Switzerland?
66510.e: A popular vote in 1866 gave Jews the right to settle freely. After that many families moved from Endingen and Lengnau to towns such as Baden and Zurich.
66510.m: Since 1866 Jews have been allowed to live anywhere in Switzerland.

66511.q: According to Hindu tradition, how many Vedas are there?
66511.e: The four Vedas are called the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda.

66512.q: Which Veda is considered the oldest?
66512.e: The Rigveda is a collection of hymns and was probably composed from around 1500 to 1200 BC.
66512.m: The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas.

66513.q: What does the word “Veda” mean when translated?

66514.q: How were the Vedas passed on for many centuries?
66514.e: Priests learnt the verses exactly by heart and passed them on orally to pupils, long before they were written down.
66514.m: For a long time the Vedas were only passed on orally.

66515.q: What does the Rigveda mainly contain?
66515.e: The Rigveda is made up of over a thousand hymns praising gods such as Indra, Agni and Varuna.
66515.m: The Rigveda is a collection of hymns.

66516.q: Which god of fire is often called upon in the Vedas?
66516.e: Agni is the god of fire and, according to Vedic belief, carries the offerings to the gods.
66516.m: Agni is the Vedic god of fire.

66517.q: In which ancient language were the Vedas composed?
66517.e: The Vedas are composed in an old form of Sanskrit. Sanskrit is the holy language of Hinduism.
66517.m: The Vedas are composed in Sanskrit.

66518.q: What role does Brahma have in the divine trinity, the Trimurti?
66518.e: In the Trimurti, Brahma creates the world, Vishnu preserves it and Shiva destroys it so that something new can arise.
66518.m: Brahma is seen as the creator of the world.

66519.q: How many heads does Brahma have in most images?
66519.e: Brahma is usually shown with four heads looking in all four directions.

66520.e: Brahma's mount is the hamsa, a swan or goose, a sign of purity and wisdom.

66521.e: Saraswati is the goddess of wisdom, music and the arts and belongs with Brahma.
66521.m: Saraswati is the goddess of wisdom and Brahma's companion.

66522.q: According to a well-known legend, what was Brahma born from?
66522.e: According to the legend, a lotus flower grows from Vishnu's navel, and Brahma appears in it.
66522.m: Brahma appeared in a lotus flower.

66523.q: Why are there only very few temples for Brahma in India?
a: He is seen as a demon
66523.e: Although Brahma is important as the creator, he is hardly worshipped in everyday life; Vishnu and Shiva have many more followers.
66523.m: Brahma is rarely worshipped in temples of his own.

66524.q: In which place in Rajasthan is the most famous Brahma temple?
66524.e: The Brahma temple in Pushkar by the holy lake is one of the few large temples for Brahma.
66524.m: The best-known Brahma temple is in Pushkar.

66525.q: What role does Vishnu have in the Trimurti?
66525.e: Vishnu keeps the order of the world and steps in when evil gets the upper hand.
66525.m: Vishnu is the preserver of the world.

66526.q: According to Hindu belief, what does Vishnu do when evil becomes too strong on earth?
a: He comes to earth in a new form
66526.e: Vishnu appears on earth again and again in new forms to save the good. These appearances are called avatars.
66526.m: Vishnu comes to earth in different forms.

66527.e: Garuda is a mighty bird, half eagle and half human, and carries Vishnu through the air.

66528.q: According to mythology, what does Vishnu rest on in the cosmic ocean?
66528.e: Vishnu rests on the many-headed snake Shesha, which floats on the cosmic ocean.
66528.m: Vishnu rests on the world snake Shesha.

66529.e: Lakshmi is the goddess of good fortune and wealth and Vishnu's wife.

66530.q: Which disc-shaped weapon does Vishnu hold in one hand?
66530.e: The Sudarshana Chakra is a spinning throwing disc and one of Vishnu's symbols.
66530.m: Vishnu carries a throwing disc, the chakra.

66531.q: Apart from the chakra, what does Vishnu often hold in another hand?
66531.e: Vishnu carries a conch shell, the shankha, whose sound is meant to drive away evil; he also has a mace and a lotus.
66531.m: The conch shell is a symbol of Vishnu.

66532.q: Which well-known heroes are seen in Hinduism as appearances of Vishnu?
66532.e: Krishna and Rama are seen as avatars, that is earthly appearances of Vishnu. Those who worship Vishnu as the highest god belong to Vaishnavism.
66532.m: Krishna and Rama are appearances of Vishnu.

66533.q: What role does Shiva have in the Trimurti?
66533.e: Shiva destroys the old so that something new can arise; that is why he is also seen as a renewer.
66533.m: Shiva destroys so that something new can arise.

66534.q: Which three-pointed weapon does Shiva carry?
66534.e: The trident is called the trishula and is Shiva's best-known symbol.

66535.e: The white bull Nandi is Shiva's mount; his statue often stands in front of Shiva temples.
66535.m: Shiva rides on the bull Nandi.

66536.q: What does Shiva have on his forehead in many pictures?
66536.e: Shiva's third eye stands for insight; according to the legend, when he opens it, it can burn everything up.
66536.m: Shiva has a third eye on his forehead.

66537.q: What does Shiva do in his form as Nataraja?
66537.e: As Nataraja, King of Dance, Shiva dances in a ring of fire the dance that destroys and recreates the world.
66537.m: As Nataraja, Shiva is the King of Dance.

66538.q: According to the legend, which holy river flows from Shiva's hair?
66538.e: Shiva caught the goddess Ganga in his hair so that her fall from heaven would not destroy the earth.
66538.m: According to the legend, the Ganges flows from Shiva's hair.

66539.q: According to belief, in which mountain range does Shiva live?
66539.e: Mount Kailash in the Himalayas in Tibet is seen as Shiva's home and is an important place of pilgrimage.
66539.m: According to belief, Shiva lives in the Himalayas.

66540.q: Why does Shiva have a blue throat in some pictures?
66540.e: Shiva drank the world poison that came out when the ocean of milk was churned, and so saved the world; it turned his throat blue.
66540.m: Shiva's blue throat comes from the poison he drank for the world.

66541.q: What does the word “avatar” mean in Hinduism?
66541.e: An avatar is a form in which a god comes down to earth to restore order.
66541.m: An avatar is the descent of a god to earth.

66542.q: How many main avatars of Vishnu does the best-known list count?
66542.e: The well-known list of the ten avatars is called the Dashavatara.
66542.m: According to the best-known list, Vishnu has ten main avatars.

66543.q: As his first avatar, Matsya, as which animal did Vishnu save people from a flood?
66543.e: As the fish Matsya, Vishnu warned the forefather Manu about the great flood and pulled his boat to safety.
66543.m: Vishnu's first avatar, Matsya, was a fish.

66544.q: In which form did Vishnu, as Kurma, carry a mountain on his back?
66544.e: As the tortoise Kurma, Vishnu held up the mountain with which gods and demons churned the ocean of milk.
66544.m: As the tortoise Kurma, Vishnu carried a mountain.

66545.q: What does Narasimha, an avatar of Vishnu, look like?
66545.e: Narasimha is a man-lion; he defeated the demon king Hiranyakashipu and protected his devout son Prahlada.
66545.m: Narasimha is half man and half lion.

66546.q: How did the dwarf Vamana cross the whole world?
66546.e: Vamana asked the demon king Bali for as much land as he could measure in three steps, and then grew to giant size.
66546.m: The dwarf Vamana crossed the world in three steps.

66547.q: According to belief, which avatar of Vishnu is still to appear in the future?
66547.e: Kalki is meant to appear on a white horse at the end of the present age and put an end to evil.
66547.m: Kalki is the future avatar of Vishnu.

66548.q: Which two very popular gods are seen as avatars of Vishnu?
66548.e: Rama is the seventh and Krishna the eighth avatar of Vishnu; both are especially worshipped all over India.
66548.m: Rama and Krishna are avatars of Vishnu.

66549.q: In which ancient language of India was the Ramayana composed?
66549.e: The Ramayana is an epic in Sanskrit. It is credited to the sage Valmiki.
66549.m: The Ramayana is an ancient epic in Sanskrit.

66550.q: What is the name of Rama's wife in the Ramayana?
66550.e: Sita is Rama's wife; her kidnapping sets off the main story of the epic.

66551.q: Who kidnaps Sita in the Ramayana?
66551.e: Ravana, the demon king of Lanka, carries Sita off to his kingdom. This starts the great battle of the epic.
66551.m: The demon king Ravana kidnaps Sita.

66552.q: For how many years does Rama have to go into exile in the forest?
66552.e: Because of a promise made by his father, Rama has to live in the forest for 14 years; Sita and his brother Lakshmana go with him.
66552.m: Rama lives in exile for 14 years.

66553.q: Which monkey god helps Rama find Sita?
66553.e: Hanuman leaps over the sea to Lanka, finds Sita and helps in the battle against Ravana.
66553.m: The monkey god Hanuman is Rama's loyal helper.

66554.q: Who is Rama in the Ramayana?
66554.e: Rama is the eldest son of King Dasharatha of Ayodhya in northern India.

66555.q: According to the Ramayana, how many heads does Ravana have?
66555.e: Ravana is shown with ten heads, which stand for his great learning and power.

66556.q: What is often burnt at the festival of Dussehra in northern India?
66556.e: Dussehra celebrates Rama's victory over Ravana; huge Ravana figures are burnt with fireworks.
66556.m: At Dussehra figures of Ravana are burnt.

66557.q: Which country does the great epic Mahabharata come from?
66557.e: The Mahabharata is one of the most important works of India. It is credited to the sage Vyasa.

66558.q: What kind of head does the god Ganesha have, who according to the legend wrote down the Mahabharata?
66558.e: Ganesha is the god with an elephant's head. According to the legend, he wrote down the whole epic without a break while Vyasa recited it.
66558.m: Ganesha with the elephant's head wrote down the Mahabharata.

66559.q: What is the Mahabharata famous for, among other things?
a: It is one of the longest epics in the world
It is the shortest poem in India
66559.e: With about 100,000 couplets, the Mahabharata is much longer than the Iliad and the Odyssey put together.
66559.m: The Mahabharata is one of the longest epics in the world.

66560.q: How many brothers make up the Pandavas in the Mahabharata?
66560.e: The five Pandava brothers are Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva.

66561.q: Who do the Pandava brothers fight against in the Mahabharata?
66561.e: The Kauravas are the hundred sons of the blind King Dhritarashtra and cousins of the Pandavas. The quarrel over the kingdom leads to war.
66561.m: The Pandavas fight their cousins, the Kauravas.

66562.q: Who wins the great battle in the Mahabharata?
a: Nobody, it ends in a draw
66562.e: The deciding battle on the field of Kurukshetra ends with victory for the Pandavas.
66562.m: The Pandavas win the great battle.

66563.q: Roughly how long does the great battle in the Mahabharata last?
66563.e: The battle of Kurukshetra lasts 18 days and ends with victory for the Pandavas.
66563.m: The battle in the Mahabharata lasts 18 days.

66564.q: In the Mahabharata, which god drives the chariot of the archer Arjuna?
66564.e: Krishna serves as Arjuna's charioteer and gives him important teachings before the battle.

66565.q: To which god is the city of Varanasi especially dedicated?
66565.e: Varanasi is seen as Shiva's city; the Kashi Vishwanath Temple is one of his most important temples.
66565.m: Varanasi is the holy city of Shiva.

66566.q: What are the wide stone steps on the riverbank in Varanasi called?
66566.e: The ghats are steps that lead down to the Ganges; believers bathe and pray there.
66566.m: The riverbank steps in Varanasi are called ghats.

66567.q: On which holy river does Varanasi lie?
66567.e: Varanasi lies on the Ganges, the holiest river of the Hindus. The city is also called Kashi, “the shining one”.
66567.m: Varanasi lies on the holy river Ganges.

66568.q: What happens at ghats such as the Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi?
66568.e: At the Manikarnika Ghat fires burn almost without stopping, on which the dead are cremated.
66568.m: The dead are cremated at the Manikarnika Ghat.

66569.q: Why do many Hindus want to die in Varanasi?
a: They hope to be freed from the cycle of rebirth
66569.e: According to belief, whoever dies in Varanasi is freed from the cycle of rebirths.
66569.m: Whoever dies in Varanasi hopes to be set free.

66570.q: What do priests do every evening by the Ganges in Varanasi?
a: A fire ceremony with oil lamps
66570.e: At the Ganga Aarti priests swing large oil lamps to chants and bells to honour the river.
66570.m: Every evening priests honour the Ganges with a fire ceremony.

66571.q: In which part of India is Varanasi?
a: On an island in the sea
66571.e: Varanasi is in the north of India in the state of Uttar Pradesh, on the plain by the Ganges.
66571.m: Varanasi is in the north of India.

66572.q: Apart from Hinduism, for which religion is the area around Varanasi also very important?
66572.e: In Sarnath, only about 10 kilometres from Varanasi, the Buddha gave his first teaching, according to tradition.
66572.m: The Buddha gave his first teaching near Varanasi.

66573.q: What does samsara mean in Hinduism?
a: The cycle of birth, death and rebirth
66573.e: Samsara is the cycle in which the soul is born again and again in a new body after death.
66573.m: Samsara is the cycle of rebirths.

66574.q: According to Hindu belief, what mainly decides the next birth?
66574.e: Good and bad deeds leave effects, called karma, and these influence the next life.

66575.q: What does the Sanskrit word “karma” literally mean?
66575.e: Karma means “deed”; the idea is that every action has consequences for the future.
